entries.title: Inglizcha gap skeleti
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Ingliz tilida odatiy xabar gap qat’iy S+V+(O/C) tartibida keladi: subject=ega, verb=kesim, object=to‘ldiruvchi, complement=kesimning izohlovchi qismi.
entries.explanationEn: An ordinary statement normally places its subject before its finite verb; objects and complements follow the appropriate verb pattern.
entries.pattern: Subject + verb + object/complement
entries.tipUz: “Reads she books” oddiy xabar gap emas; o‘zbekcha tartibni ko‘chirmang.

examples.en: She reads books.
We study English.
The room feels warm.

entries.title: So‘z turkumlari
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb, preposition, determiner, conjunction, interjection kabi sinflar vazifasiga ko‘ra farqlanadi. Bir so‘z turli kontekstda turkumini o‘zgartirishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Word class depends on how a word functions in its sentence, not just its spelling.
entries.pattern: a fast car (adjective); drive fast (adverb)
entries.tipUz: “Hard” va “hardly” bir ma’noda emas: hardly=deyarli ... emas.

examples.en: They work hard.
The train is fast.
The train moves fast.

entries.title: Ega va kesim
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: To‘liq mustaqil gapda odatda ega va finite (shaxs/zamon ko‘rsatadigan) fe’l bor; buyruqda “you” yashirin bo‘lishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: A full independent clause normally needs a subject and a finite verb; an imperative can leave its subject understood.
entries.pattern: Subject + finite verb; imperative: (You) + base verb
entries.tipUz: “Very beautiful.” odatda mustaqil to‘liq gap emas, fragment.

examples.en: The sun rises.
My brother works.
Please wait here.

entries.title: To be: am/is/are
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Hozirgi zamonda holat, sifat, kasb va joyni ifodalaydi; olmoshga qarab am/is/are tanlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Present forms of be connect the subject to an identity, state or place; match am, is and are to the subject.
entries.pattern: I am; he/she/it is; we/you/they are
entries.tipUz: “I ready” noto‘g‘ri: inglizcha adjectivedan oldin bu yerda be kerak.

examples.en: I am ready.
She is a teacher.
We are at home.

entries.title: Be: inkor va savol
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Be fe’li bilan not be dan so‘ng, savolda esa be egadan oldin keladi.
entries.explanationEn: Put not after be for a negative, and put be before the subject for an ordinary yes/no question.
entries.pattern: S + be + not; Be + S + ...?
entries.tipUz: “Do you are?” emas, “Are you?” bo‘ladi.

examples.en: Is she at home?
They are not ready.
Are you tired?

entries.title: Olmoshlar: I/me/my/mine
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Subject va object olmoshlari o‘rin bo‘yicha farqlanadi; possessive determiner otdan oldin, possessive pronoun mustaqil ishlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Subject, object, possessive determiner and possessive pronoun forms occupy different positions.
entries.pattern: I–me–my–mine; she–her–her–hers
entries.tipUz: “Mine bag” emas, “my bag”.

examples.en: This is my bag; it is mine.
She gave it to me.
This pen is hers.

entries.title: Birlik va ko‘plik
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Ko‘p sanaladigan otlarga -s/-es qo‘shiladi; irregular ko‘pliklar alohida o‘rganiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Countable nouns can be singular or plural; regular endings and irregular plural forms must be distinguished.
entries.pattern: book→books; child→children; mouse→mice
entries.tipUz: “Two childs” emas; sheep va fish ba’zan o‘zgarmaydi.

examples.en: Two children are here.
Three women are waiting.
These boxes are heavy.

entries.title: A/an tushunchasi
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Noma’lum birlik sanaladigan ot oldida a/an ishlatiladi; tanlov harfga emas, tovushga bog‘liq.
entries.explanationEn: Choose a or an by the first pronounced sound of a singular countable expression.
entries.pattern: a university /ən/ emas /juː/; an hour (h ovozsiz)
entries.tipUz: “I am student” emas, “I am a student”.

examples.en: She is an engineer.
He is a university student.
We waited for an hour.

entries.title: The tushunchasi
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Tinglovchi uchun ma’lum, oldin tilga olingan yoki noyob referent uchun the ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: The commonly identifies a referent the listener can locate in context; it is not required before every noun.
entries.pattern: a book → the book
entries.tipUz: “The” har bir otga qo‘yilmaydi.

examples.en: I found a key; the key was rusty.
Please close the door.
I bought a book. The book was useful.
examples.uz: Kitob oldim. O‘sha kitob foydali ekan.

entries.title: This/that/these/those
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Yaqin/uzoq hamda birlik/ko‘plik referentlarni ko‘rsatadi.
entries.explanationEn: Demonstratives distinguish singular/plural and contextually nearer/more distant referents.
entries.pattern: this/these (yaqin), that/those (uzoq)
entries.tipUz: “This shoes” emas, “these shoes”.

examples.en: These shoes are new.
This chair is comfortable.
Those houses are old.

entries.title: Have/has
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Egalik va xususiyatni bildiradi; he/she/it bilan has ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: For present possession, use has with third-person singular subjects and have with the other ordinary subjects.
entries.pattern: I/you/we/they have; he/she/it has
entries.tipUz: “She have” oddiy presentda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: My sister has a bike.
We have enough time.
The house has two doors.

entries.title: There is/are
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Mavjudlikni bildiradi; undan keyingi otning soni bilan moslashadi.
entries.explanationEn: Existential there introduces something present or existing; standard agreement follows the introduced noun phrase.
entries.pattern: There is + singular; There are + plural
entries.tipUz: “It is three chairs” mavjudlik ifodasi emas.

examples.en: There are three chairs.
There is a park nearby.
There are two messages.

entries.title: Asosiy so‘roq so‘zlar
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Who/what/where/when/why/how savolning maqsadini belgilaydi; odatda yordamchi fe’l tartibi saqlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: A wh-word identifies the information sought; the remaining question still follows its appropriate auxiliary pattern.
entries.pattern: Wh-word + auxiliary/be + subject + ...?
entries.tipUz: “Where you live?” standart savol emas, ayrim norasmiy kontekstlar bundan mustasno.

examples.en: Where do you live?
When does the lesson start?
Why are you waiting?

entries.title: And, but, or
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Ikki teng birlikni bog‘laydi: and=qo‘shish, but=zidlik, or=tanlov.
entries.explanationEn: And adds, but contrasts, and or offers alternatives; coordinate elements with compatible grammatical roles.
entries.pattern: X and Y; X but Y; X or Y
entries.tipUz: Vergulni gaplar tuzilishi, uzunligi va ma’nosiga qarab tanlang; har ikki qisqa clause orasida majburiy emas.

examples.en: I was tired, but I studied.
She reads and writes.
Would you like tea or water?

entries.title: In/on/at boshlang‘ich
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: In=ichida/keng vaqt; on=sirt/kun; at=nuqta/aniq vaqt. Bu faqat boshlang‘ich model: ko‘plab idiomatik birikmalar bor.
entries.explanationEn: In, on and at have common place/time patterns, but individual combinations also need to be learned.
entries.pattern: in the room; on Monday; at six
entries.tipUz: “In Monday” emas, “on Monday”.

examples.en: We meet at six on Friday.
The keys are on the table.
The class starts at nine.

entries.title: Oddiy inkor
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Be bo‘lmagan oddiy fe’llar presentda do/does not yordamchisiga muhtoj; asosiy fe’l base shaklida qoladi.
entries.explanationEn: In ordinary present negatives without another auxiliary, use do/does not and the base verb.
entries.pattern: I don't work; he doesn't work
entries.tipUz: “Doesn't smokes” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: He doesn't smoke.
I do not drive.
She does not work here.

entries.title: Katta harf va asosiy punktuatsiya
entries.chapter: 01  A0  |  Tilning anatomiyasi va noldan boshlash
entries.explanationUz: Gap boshida, I olmoshida, atoqli otlarda bosh harf; xabar uchun nuqta, savol uchun so‘roq belgisi ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Capitalise sentence beginnings, I and appropriate proper names; punctuation marks the intended sentence type.
entries.pattern: My name is Ali. / Is it true?
entries.tipUz: Inglizcha “i” emas, doimo “I”.

examples.en: I live in Uzbekistan.
My name is Lola.
Is Monday convenient?

entries.title: Present simple: odat va fakt
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Odat, jadval, umumiy haqiqat uchun present simple ishlatiladi; 3-shaxs birlikda -s/-es.
entries.explanationEn: Present simple commonly describes habits, schedules and general states; third-person singular adds its appropriate ending.
entries.pattern: S + V(s/es)
entries.tipUz: “She study” yoki “She does studies” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: She studies every day.
He walks to work.
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius under ordinary pressure.
examples.uz: Odatdagi bosimda suv Selsiy bo‘yicha nol darajada muzlaydi.

entries.title: Present simple savol
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Do/does egadan oldinga chiqadi va asosiy fe’l boshlang‘ich shaklga qaytadi.
entries.explanationEn: Do/does carries the question agreement, leaving the main verb in its base form.
entries.pattern: Do/Does + S + base verb?
entries.tipUz: He plays, ammo Does he play?

examples.en: Does he play chess?
Do they study here?
Where does she work?

entries.title: Present continuous
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Hozir ayni damda/vaqtincha davom etayotgan jarayon uchun be + -ing.
entries.explanationEn: Present continuous combines present be with an -ing form for an ongoing or temporary activity.
entries.pattern: S + am/is/are + V-ing
entries.tipUz: “I reading” emas; ko‘p stative fe’llar continuous ishlatmaydi.

examples.en: I am reading now.
She is writing a letter.
We are staying with friends this week.

entries.title: Present simple vs continuous
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Doimiy odat va ayni paytdagi faoliyatni kontekst ajratadi.
entries.explanationEn: Choose the simple or progressive according to the intended habitual, general, ongoing or temporary meaning.
entries.pattern: I work / I'm working
entries.tipUz: “Every day” bilan odatda simple, “right now” bilan continuous.

examples.en: I work in a bank, but I'm working from home today.
examples.uz: Bankda ishlayman, lekin bugun uydan ishlayapman.

examples.en: She usually walks, but today she is taking the bus.
examples.uz: U odatda piyoda yuradi, bugun esa avtobusda ketyapti.

examples.en: I read every evening. I am reading now.
examples.uz: Har oqshom o‘qiyman. Hozir ham o‘qiyapman.

entries.title: Past simple regular
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishda yakunlangan hodisa uchun V-ed; did bilan savol/inkorda base form.
entries.explanationEn: Regular past forms commonly end in -ed; did already marks the past in questions and negatives.
entries.pattern: S + V-ed; Did + S + V?
entries.tipUz: “Did you visited?” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: We visited Samarkand yesterday.
She cleaned her room yesterday.
Did you finish the task?

entries.title: Past simple irregular
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Go→went, buy→bought, see→saw kabi fe’llarni yodlash lozim.
entries.explanationEn: Irregular past forms are lexical patterns to learn, not forms made by adding -ed to every verb.
entries.pattern: S + V2
entries.tipUz: “She goed” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: She went home early.
I bought some bread.
They saw a bird.

entries.title: Was/were
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Be fe’lining o'tgan shakli: I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were.
entries.explanationEn: Use was/were for past be, matching the subject; do not add did to an ordinary be question.
entries.pattern: S + was/were (+ not)
entries.tipUz: “Did she was?” emas, “Was she?”.

examples.en: They were tired.
I was at home.
Were you busy yesterday?

entries.title: Will: oddiy kelajak
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Tez qaror, taxmin, va’da kabi ma’nolarda will + base verb qo‘llanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Will plus a base verb can express decisions, predictions or promises; context determines the meaning.
entries.pattern: S + will + V
entries.tipUz: “Will goes” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: I'll call you later.
I will help you.
It will be cold tonight.

entries.title: Be going to
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Oldindan rejalashtirilgan niyat yoki ko‘rinib turgan dalilga asoslangan prognoz.
entries.explanationEn: Be going to commonly presents an intention or a prediction grounded in visible evidence.
entries.pattern: am/is/are going to + V
entries.tipUz: “I going to” emas, “I am going to”.

examples.en: It is going to rain.
We are going to study together.
Look at the clouds. It is going to rain.

entries.title: Can/can't
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Qobiliyat, ruxsat, imkon ma’nolarida can + V; uchinchi shaxsda ham -s qo‘shilmaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Can takes a base verb without third-person -s and can express ability, permission or possibility.
entries.pattern: S + can + base verb
entries.tipUz: “Can swims” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: She can swim.
Can I sit here?
He cannot drive.

entries.title: Imperative
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Buyruq, ko‘rsatma yoki iltimosda ega ko‘pincha aytilmaydi, fe’l base shaklda turadi.
entries.explanationEn: An imperative usually uses a base verb with an understood you; do not makes an ordinary negative imperative.
entries.pattern: Open the door; Don't open the door
entries.tipUz: “You sit down” boshqa urg‘u beradi.

examples.en: Please sit down.
Turn left at the corner.
Do not touch the screen.

entries.title: Countable va uncountable
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Countable ot sanaladi: a chair/two chairs; uncountable: information/water.
entries.explanationEn: Countability depends on the noun's sense; mass nouns commonly need a measure expression for individual units.
entries.pattern: a piece of information; some water
entries.tipUz: “An advice” emas, “a piece of advice”.

examples.en: I need some advice.
There are three chairs.
Could I have a glass of water?

entries.title: Some/any
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Tasdiqda some, ko‘p so‘roq va inkorda any; taklif va iltimoslarda some ham bo‘ladi.
entries.explanationEn: Some and any vary with polarity, expectation and communicative purpose, including offers and requests.
entries.pattern: some apples; any apples
entries.tipUz: “Would you like some tea?” tabiiy taklif.

examples.en: Do you have any questions?
We have some apples.
Would you like some water?

entries.title: Much/many/a lot of
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Many sanaladigan ko‘plik, much sanalmaydigan ot bilan; a lot of ikkisida ham ishlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Many combines with plural count nouns, much with mass nouns, and a lot of can combine with either.
entries.pattern: many books; much time; a lot of time/books
entries.tipUz: “Much people” emas, “many people”.

examples.en: We don't have much time.
There are many reasons.
We have a lot of work.

entries.title: Adjectives va tartib
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Oddiy sifat otdan oldin yoki linking verbdan keyin keladi.
entries.explanationEn: An adjective commonly comes before a noun or after a linking verb, rather than simply following its noun.
entries.pattern: a beautiful city; the city is beautiful
entries.tipUz: “A book interesting” standart tartib emas.

examples.en: It is an interesting book.
She has a red bag.
The bag is red.

entries.title: Adverbs of frequency
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Always/usually/often/sometimes/never odatda main fe’ldan oldin, be dan keyin keladi.
entries.explanationEn: Frequency adverbs commonly precede lexical verbs but follow be; focus and context permit variation.
entries.pattern: S + often + V; S + be + often
entries.tipUz: “She arrives usually” ko‘p kontekstda g‘ayritabiiy.

examples.en: She usually arrives early.
I often read at night.
He is always polite.

entries.title: Place/time adverbs
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Joy va vaqt holi ko‘pincha oxirda keladi; joy odatda vaqtdan oldin.
entries.explanationEn: Place and time adjuncts often appear near the end, with place before time, but discourse can change the order.
entries.pattern: S + V + place + time
entries.tipUz: Barcha hol tartiblari qat’iy emas: urg‘u tartibni o‘zgartiradi.

examples.en: We studied at home yesterday.
They met in the park on Sunday.
Yesterday we worked at home.

entries.title: Object pronouns
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Me/him/her/us/them fe’l va predlogdan so‘ng keladi.
entries.explanationEn: Object pronouns commonly follow verbs or prepositions; they do not replace subject pronouns indiscriminately.
entries.pattern: verb/preposition + object pronoun
entries.tipUz: “Help I” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Please help me.
She called him.
This gift is for them.

entries.title: Possessive 's
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Odatda odamlar, hayvonlar, vaqt va guruhlar egaligida ’s qo‘llanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Possessive apostrophes differ between ordinary singular nouns, regular plurals and irregular plurals.
entries.pattern: Ali's book; the children's toys
entries.tipUz: Ko‘plik -s bilan tugasa: students' books.

examples.en: My mother's car is old.
The teacher's desk is new.
The students' bags are outside.

entries.title: Wh-questions va subject questions
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Subjectni so‘rashda ko‘pincha do-support kerak emas.
entries.explanationEn: When who/what is the subject, ordinary do-support is absent; object questions have a different structure.
entries.pattern: Who came? vs Who did you see?
entries.tipUz: “Who did break the window?” oddiy neytral subject question emas (urg‘uda mumkin).

examples.en: Who broke the window?
Who called you?
Who did you call?

entries.title: Comparatives
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Qisqa sifat + -er, ko‘p uzun sifatlarda more; than bilan taqqoslanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Use a suitable comparative form, with than when the comparison explicitly names its second term.
entries.pattern: faster than; more useful than
entries.tipUz: “More easier” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: This route is shorter.
This bag is lighter than mine.
The new method is more reliable.

entries.title: Superlatives
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Eng yuqori daraja: the + -est yoki the most; irregular: good–better–best.
entries.explanationEn: Superlatives identify an extreme within a relevant group; irregular forms need separate learning.
entries.pattern: the fastest; the most reliable
entries.tipUz: “The most fastest” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: It is the best option.
This is the smallest room.
She chose the most practical option.

entries.title: Prepositions of movement
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: To yo‘nalish, into ichkariga, onto sirtga, from kelib chiqishni bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Movement prepositions distinguish destination, entry, movement onto a surface and origin.
entries.pattern: go to / walk into / jump onto
entries.tipUz: “Arrive to” odatda emas: arrive at/in.

examples.en: She walked into the room.
He jumped onto the platform.
We walked from school to the park.

entries.title: Like/love/hate + -ing
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Umumiy faoliyatni yoqtirishni -ing bilan ifodalash juda ko‘p; ayrim fe’llar to-infinitive ham oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Verb complementation is lexical: enjoy takes -ing, while like can allow different patterns according to meaning.
entries.pattern: enjoy + -ing; like + -ing/to V
entries.tipUz: “Enjoy to cook” standart emas.

examples.en: I enjoy cooking.
They love walking.
I like to check my work before sending it.
examples.uz: Ishni yuborishdan oldin tekshirishni ma’qul ko‘raman.

entries.title: Because/so
entries.chapter: 02  A1  |  Birinchi mustaqil gaplar
entries.explanationUz: Because sababni, so natijani kiritadi.
entries.explanationEn: Because introduces a reason, while so can connect that reason to its result.
entries.pattern: result because reason; reason, so result
entries.tipUz: “Because ..., so ...” ni bitta bog‘lanishda ortiqcha qo‘llamang.

examples.en: I stayed in because it was cold.
Because I was busy, I stayed home.
The road was closed, so we waited.
examples.uz: Yo‘l yopiq edi, shuning uchun kutdik.

entries.title: Present perfect: experience/result
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Have/has + V3 o‘tmish tajribasi yoki hozirga ta’sirli natijani bildiradi; aniq tugagan vaqt bilan odatda past simple.
entries.explanationEn: Present perfect relates an earlier situation to the present; an explicitly finished past time normally favours past simple.
entries.pattern: S + have/has + V3
entries.tipUz: “I have lost ... yesterday” emas, “I lost ... yesterday”.

examples.en: I have lost my keys.
She has finished the report.
examples.uz: U hisobotni tugatdi; hozir u tayyor.

examples.en: Have you tried this dish?

entries.title: Present perfect: for/since
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: For muddatni, since boshlanish nuqtasini ko‘rsatadi; holat hozirgacha davom etishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: For measures a duration; since identifies its starting point. The wider construction determines whether the situation continues.
entries.pattern: have lived here for five years / since 2021
entries.tipUz: “Since five years” emas, “for five years”.

examples.en: We have known each other for years.
I have lived here since March.
He has worked here for two years.
examples.uz: U ikki yildan beri shu yerda ishlaydi.

entries.title: Already/yet/just/ever/never
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Natija va tajriba bilan bog‘liq vaqt ravishlari; o‘rinlari ham ahamiyatli.
entries.explanationEn: Already, yet, just, ever and never have different meanings and typical positions in perfect constructions.
entries.pattern: have just/already V3; haven't V3 yet
entries.tipUz: “Have you ever went” emas, “have you ever been/gone”.

examples.en: Have you ever been abroad?
I have just arrived.
She has not replied yet.

entries.title: Present perfect vs past simple
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Hozir bilan bog‘lanish bor-yo‘qligini va vaqtning yopiq-ochiqligini tekshiring.
entries.explanationEn: Distinguish a finished past-time frame from experience or results connected to now.
entries.pattern: I have seen it / I saw it last night
entries.tipUz: “Last year, I have visited...” standart emas.

examples.en: I visited Bukhara in 2022.
I have visited Bukhara twice.
I visited Bukhara last summer.

entries.title: Past continuous
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishda muayyan vaqtda davom etayotgan jarayon yoki fon holati.
entries.explanationEn: Past continuous presents an activity in progress at a past reference point, often as background.
entries.pattern: was/were + V-ing
entries.tipUz: Fon=continuous, qisqa aralashuv ko‘pincha past simple.

examples.en: I was studying when you called.
They were eating when I arrived.
At nine, she was studying.

entries.title: Past simple vs past continuous
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Ikki amal navbatma-navbat sodir bo‘lsa past simple; bir amal fonda davom etsa continuous.
entries.explanationEn: Past simple can narrate successive events, while past continuous can present background activity; while is not an automatic tense rule.
entries.pattern: While I was cooking, the phone rang
entries.tipUz: “While” har doim continuous talab qilmaydi.

examples.en: She fell while she was running.
I opened the door and sat down.
While we were talking, the lights went out.

entries.title: Future arrangements
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Present continuous kelishilgan yaqin kelajak rejalarida ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Present continuous can refer to an arranged future activity when context supplies the future time.
entries.pattern: am/is/are + V-ing + future time
entries.tipUz: Jadval uchun present simple ham mumkin: The train leaves at eight.

examples.en: I'm meeting my tutor tomorrow.
We are having lunch together tomorrow.
She is leaving on Friday.

entries.title: Future time clauses
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: When/after/before/as soon as/until dan keyin kelajak ma’nosida odatda will emas, present form ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: In ordinary future time clauses, a present form follows when/after/until rather than a future will form.
entries.pattern: When + present, will + V
entries.tipUz: “When I will arrive” oddiy vaqt gapida noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: I'll text you when I arrive.
We will start after he arrives.
Wait until the light turns green.

entries.title: Must vs have to
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Must kuchli talab/so‘zlovchi nuqtayi nazari, have to tashqi majburiyat uchun ko‘p ishlatiladi; chegaralar kontekstga bog‘liq.
entries.explanationEn: Must and have to overlap in obligation, but must not means prohibition and do not have to means absence of necessity.
entries.pattern: must + V; have to + V
entries.tipUz: Mustn't=taqiq, don't have to=zarur emas.

examples.en: I have to wear a uniform.
You must not park here.
You do not have to come early.

entries.title: Should/ought to
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Maslahat va kutilgan to‘g‘ri yo‘lni bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Should and ought to commonly express advice or expectation; should does not take to.
entries.pattern: should/ought to + V
entries.tipUz: “Should to study” emas, “should study”.

examples.en: You should revise regularly.
You ought to check the address.
She should arrive soon.
examples.uz: U tez orada yetib kelishi kerak.

entries.title: May/might/could
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Ehtimolni ko‘rsatadi; may/might va epistemic could orasidagi nozik farqlar kontekstga bog‘liq.
entries.explanationEn: May, might and could can express possibility; their strength and negative interpretations depend on context.
entries.pattern: It may/might/could + V
entries.tipUz: Might not — ehtimol bunday emas yoki bo‘lmaydi; can’t esa xulosa ma’nosida ko‘pincha imkonsizlikni bildiradi.

examples.en: It might snow tonight.
They may be at home.
The answer could be different.

entries.title: Could vs was able to
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Umumiy o‘tmish qobiliyati uchun could; aniq bir muvaffaqiyatli natija uchun was able to/managed to ko‘proq ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Could commonly describes past general ability; managed to/was able to often suits one successful event.
entries.pattern: could swim / managed to escape
entries.tipUz: Tasdiqdagi yagona muvaffaqiyat “could” bilan har doim tabiiy emas.

examples.en: We managed to finish on time.
I could swim when I was young.
She was able to open the door.

entries.title: Used to
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Ilgari odat bo‘lgan, hozir esa odatda davom etmaydigan holat/odat.
entries.explanationEn: Used to plus a base verb presents a former habit or state, commonly contrasted with the present.
entries.pattern: used to + V; didn't use to + V
entries.tipUz: “I am used to” boshqa: ko‘nikkanman.

examples.en: I used to live in a village.
He used to cycle to work.
We did not use to have a car.

entries.title: Be used to / get used to
aliases: Be used to / get used to
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: To bu yerda predlog: ot yoki -ing talab qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Be/get used to takes a noun or -ing form because to is a preposition in this construction.
entries.pattern: be/get used to + noun/V-ing
entries.tipUz: “Used to wake” odat, “am used to waking” ko‘nikish.

examples.en: I'm used to waking up early.
She is used to the noise.
I am getting used to working early.

entries.title: Gerund vs to-infinitive
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Ayrim fe’llardan keyin -ing (avoid, enjoy), boshqalardan keyin to V (decide, hope); ayrimlar ikkisini ma’no o‘zgarishi bilan oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Choose -ing or an infinitive according to the governing verb and intended meaning, not one universal translation rule.
entries.pattern: avoid doing; decide to do
entries.tipUz: Bitta universal qoida yo‘q: verb patternni o‘rganing.

examples.en: She decided to apply.
We avoided making a mistake.
He hopes to return soon.
examples.uz: U tez orada qaytishga umid qiladi.

entries.title: First conditional
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Realistik kelajak ehtimoli: if + present, will/can/may + V.
entries.explanationEn: A realistic future condition commonly combines an if-present clause with a modal result clause.
entries.pattern: If + present, will + V
entries.tipUz: Oddiy shart gapida “If I will have” emas.

examples.en: If I have time, I'll help.
If she calls, I will answer.
If we leave now, we can catch the bus.

entries.title: Zero conditional
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Har safar to‘g‘ri bo‘ladigan qoidalar, ilmiy faktlar.
entries.explanationEn: A zero conditional can express a general relationship or a regularly repeated consequence, not just scientific laws.
entries.pattern: If/when + present, present
entries.tipUz: Bu qolip har doim faqat fan uchun emas, takroriy holatga ham mos.

examples.en: If water freezes, it expands.
If I feel tired, I take a break.
When the button is pressed, the light comes on.

entries.title: Second conditional
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Hozirgi/kelajakdagi faraziy yoki ehtimoli past vaziyat.
entries.explanationEn: A past form in a second conditional can mark hypothetical distance rather than past time.
entries.pattern: If + past, would + V
entries.tipUz: “If I would have” standart asosiy qolip emas.

examples.en: If I had more time, I'd travel.
If I were you, I would wait.
If she knew the answer, she would tell us.

entries.title: Relative clauses: who/which/that
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Otdan keyin uni cheklab aniqlaydigan defining clause; shaxs uchun who, narsa uchun which, ko‘pincha that.
entries.explanationEn: A defining relative identifies which person or thing is meant; its subject pronoun cannot simply be omitted.
entries.pattern: noun + who/which/that + clause
entries.tipUz: Subject relative pronounni tashlab bo‘lmaydi: “The man lives here” boshqa gap.

examples.en: The student who called is absent.
The woman who teaches us is kind.
The phone that rang is mine.

entries.title: Object relatives and omission
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Relative pronoun to‘ldiruvchi bo‘lsa defining clauseda tushirilishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: An object relative pronoun can be omitted in a defining clause; omitting a subject relative changes or breaks the structure.
entries.pattern: The book (that) I bought
entries.tipUz: “The woman who met me” va “the woman I met” ma’noda boshqa.

examples.en: The film I watched was excellent.
The book I borrowed is useful.
The person you called has arrived.

entries.title: Too/enough
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Too + adjective = haddan ortiq; adjective + enough = yetarli; enough + noun.
entries.explanationEn: Too expresses excess, while enough expresses sufficiency and follows an adjective but precedes a noun.
entries.pattern: too expensive; old enough; enough money
entries.tipUz: “Enough old” emas, “old enough”.

examples.en: It's too late to leave.
The bag is too heavy to carry.
examples.uz: Sumka ko‘tarish uchun haddan tashqari og‘ir.

examples.en: We have enough chairs.

entries.title: So/such
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: So sifat/ravishni, such otli birikmani kuchaytiradi; so ... that va such ... that natija beradi.
entries.explanationEn: So modifies an adjective/adverb; such introduces a noun phrase, often with an article for a singular count noun.
entries.pattern: so difficult / such a difficult test
entries.tipUz: “So a good idea” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: It was such a good idea.
The room was so quiet.
It was such a useful lesson.

entries.title: Comparative modifiers
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Much/far/a little/slightly kabi so‘zlar comparative oldidan darajani bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Comparatives take suitable degree modifiers such as much, far or slightly rather than an extra comparative ending.
entries.pattern: much better; slightly cheaper
entries.tipUz: “Very better” odatda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: This solution is far more effective.
This route is slightly longer.
Her answer is much clearer.

entries.title: Reflexive pronouns
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Myself/yourself/himself/themselves ish subyektning o‘ziga qaytganda yoki urg‘u uchun.
entries.explanationEn: Reflexive pronouns can identify a subject acting on itself or add emphasis; they are not ordinary subject-pronoun substitutes.
entries.pattern: She taught herself; I did it myself
entries.tipUz: “Myself went” subject o‘rnida emas.

examples.en: He hurt himself.
She introduced herself.
We repaired it ourselves.

entries.title: Each/every/all/both
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Each alohidalik, every guruh a’zolarining barchasi, all yaxlitlik, both ikkisini bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Each/every commonly takes a singular count noun; all and both select different number and grouping patterns.
entries.pattern: each student is; every student is; all students are
entries.tipUz: “Every students” emas, “every student”.

examples.en: Both options are valid.
Each student has a book.
All the students are ready.

entries.title: Either/neither
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Either ikki variantdan biri; neither ikkalasi ham emas; fe’l moslashuvi uslubga bog‘liq.
entries.explanationEn: Either selects one of two possibilities; neither excludes both. Agreement can vary with construction and register.
entries.pattern: either option; neither answer
entries.tipUz: “Neither ... or” emas, “neither ... nor”.

examples.en: Neither answer is correct.
You can choose either seat.
Neither of the doors is open.

entries.title: Question tags
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Yordamchi fe’l va ega olmoshi bilan tasdiq–inkor teskarilanadi; ohang ma’noni o‘zgartiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Canonical tags match the auxiliary and pronoun, commonly reversing polarity; intonation affects whether confirmation is expected.
entries.pattern: You're ready, aren't you?
entries.tipUz: “I'm late, aren't I?” istisno qolip.

examples.en: He doesn't drive, does he?
She is ready, isn't she?
You have finished, haven't you?

entries.title: Indirect questions
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Muloyim savolda ichki qism xabar gap tartibida keladi.
entries.explanationEn: The embedded part of an indirect question normally has statement order, not direct-question inversion.
entries.pattern: Could you tell me + where + S + V?
entries.tipUz: “Do you know where does she live?” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Do you know where she lives?
Could you tell me where the station is?
I wonder why he left.

entries.title: Articles with geography
entries.chapter: 03  A2  |  Tizimli grammatik poydevor
entries.explanationUz: Mamlakatlar odatda articlesiz, daryo va ayrim birikmali nomlar the bilan; istisnolar ko‘p.
entries.explanationEn: Geographical names have conventional article patterns; countries, rivers and plural names do not all behave alike.
entries.pattern: Uzbekistan; the Nile; the United Kingdom
entries.tipUz: “The Uzbekistan” odatda emas.

examples.en: They visited the Netherlands.
The Nile is a river.
She lives in Uzbekistan.

entries.title: Present perfect continuous
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishda boshlanib hozirga qadar davom etayotgan jarayon yoki ko‘rinadigan natijaning davomiyligini ko‘rsatadi.
entries.explanationEn: Present perfect continuous highlights an activity extending towards now or its present evidence; not every state takes -ing.
entries.pattern: have/has been + V-ing
entries.tipUz: Stative know odatda “I've known”, “I've been knowing” emas.

examples.en: I've been studying for two hours.
She has been working all morning.
It has been raining.
examples.uz: Yomg‘ir yog‘ib turibdi; uning hozirgi izi yoki davomiyligi nazarda tutilgan.

entries.title: Present perfect simple vs continuous
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Simple ko‘pincha tugallangan son/natijani, continuous vaqt va jarayonni urg‘ulaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Perfect simple often highlights completion or quantity; perfect continuous often highlights the process or duration.
entries.pattern: have written three emails / have been writing all morning
entries.tipUz: “How long?” bilan perfect continuous tez-tez, lekin har doim emas.

examples.en: She has written five pages.
I have read three chapters.
I have been reading for an hour.

entries.title: Past perfect
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishdagi boshqa nuqtadan ilgari sodir bo‘lgan ish; shunchaki har qanday o‘tmishga past perfect shart emas.
entries.explanationEn: Past perfect locates a situation before a past reference point; it is not obligatory for every past event.
entries.pattern: had + V3
entries.tipUz: Tartib ravshan bo‘lsa past simple ham yetarli bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: By the time I arrived, they had left.
She had eaten before we arrived.
examples.uz: Biz kelishimizdan oldin u ovqatlanib bo‘lgan edi.

examples.en: I realised I had lost my ticket.

entries.title: Past perfect continuous
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishdagi nuqtagacha davom etib kelgan jarayon/uning natijasi.
entries.explanationEn: Past perfect continuous looks back from a past point at an activity's duration or continuing effects.
entries.pattern: had been + V-ing
entries.tipUz: Uzoq muddatli stative fe’llarni avtomatik -ing qilmang.

examples.en: She had been waiting for an hour.
examples.uz: U bir soatdan beri kutayotgan edi.

examples.en: We had been walking for hours before we stopped.
He was tired because he had been working.
examples.uz: Ishlab kelgani uchun u charchagan edi.

entries.title: Future continuous
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Kelajakning muayyan vaqtida davom etayotgan harakat yoki muloyim so‘rov.
entries.explanationEn: Future continuous presents an activity in progress at a future point and can also make an enquiry less direct.
entries.pattern: will be + V-ing
entries.tipUz: “Will be study” emas, “will be studying”.

examples.en: At eight, I'll be revising.
This time tomorrow, we will be travelling.
examples.uz: Ertaga shu paytda yo‘lda ketayotgan bo‘lamiz.

examples.en: Will you be using the car tonight?

entries.title: Future perfect
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Belgilangan kelajak nuqtasigacha yakunlangan harakat.
entries.explanationEn: Future perfect places completion before a specified future deadline; by and until express different time relations.
entries.pattern: will have + V3
entries.tipUz: By belgilangan muddat, until davom etish chegarasi; bir xil emas.

examples.en: By June, I'll have finished the course.
By Friday, she will have finished.
We will have left before you arrive.
examples.uz: Siz kelishingizdan oldin jo‘nab ketgan bo‘lamiz.

entries.title: Future perfect continuous
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Kelajak nuqtasigacha faoliyat qancha davom etgan bo‘lishini urg‘ulaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Future perfect continuous measures an activity's duration up to a future reference point.
entries.pattern: will have been + V-ing
entries.tipUz: Kamroq ishlatiladi; ma’no zarur bo‘lgandagina tanlang.

examples.en: By noon, I'll have been working for six hours.
By June, she will have been teaching for ten years.
examples.uz: Iyunga kelib uning dars berayotganiga o‘n yil bo‘ladi.

examples.en: At six, we will have been waiting for an hour.
examples.uz: Soat oltida kutayotganimizga bir soat bo‘ladi.

entries.title: Future in the past
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmish nuqtasidan turib kelajak bo‘lgan hodisa: would/was going to/was to.
entries.explanationEn: Future in the past presents a later event from an earlier viewpoint; would can have other meanings in other contexts.
entries.pattern: He said he would return
entries.tipUz: Would ba’zan shart/odat ham bo‘lishi mumkin; kontekst kerak.

examples.en: She knew they were going to leave.
He promised he would call.
We were going to leave, but it rained.

entries.title: Passive: present/past
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: E’tibor bajaruvchidan jarayon yoki natijaga ko‘chadi; patient ega bo‘ladi.
entries.explanationEn: A passive uses a form of be and a past participle, with its subject corresponding to an affected participant.
entries.pattern: be (tense) + V3
entries.tipUz: “Was build” emas, “was built”.

examples.en: The bridge was built in 1990.
The room is cleaned daily.
The letter was sent yesterday.

entries.title: Passive: barcha aspectlar
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Perfect/continuous/modal passiv ham mavjud; juda og‘ir shakllarni faqat kerak bo‘lsa qo‘llang.
entries.explanationEn: Passive voice combines with tense/aspect and modals in a fixed auxiliary order; heavier forms need a real communicative purpose.
entries.pattern: has been done; is being done; must be done
entries.tipUz: “Has being done” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: The issue is being investigated.
The work has been completed.
The door must be closed.

entries.title: Agent: by, instrument: with
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Passive by=kim bajardi, with=nimadan foydalanildi; agent noma’lum yoki ahamiyatsiz bo‘lsa aytilmaydi.
entries.explanationEn: By commonly names a passive agent; with commonly names an instrument. The intended relationship matters.
entries.pattern: was written by X / was cut with Y
entries.tipUz: “By a stone” instrumental ma’noda ko‘pincha mos emas.

examples.en: The window was broken with a stone.
The poem was written by a student.
The paper was cut with scissors.

entries.title: Get passive
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Ko‘pincha voqea/kutilmagan ta’sir va norasmiy uslub; get + V3.
entries.explanationEn: Get-passives often foreground an event or its effect and are common in less formal contexts; they do not replace every be-passive.
entries.pattern: get fired / get hurt
entries.tipUz: Barcha rasmiy akademik passiv o‘rniga get qo‘ymang.

examples.en: He got promoted last month.
My bag got damaged.
They got invited to the event.

entries.title: Reported speech: statements
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishdagi reporting verbdan keyin backshift (is→was, will→would) tez-tez; haqiqat hozir ham amal qilsa shart emas.
entries.explanationEn: Reported statements may backshift after a past reporting verb, but continuing truth and context can support an unshifted form.
entries.pattern: He said (that) he was tired
entries.tipUz: “He said me” emas, “he told me” yoki “he said to me”.

examples.en: She said she had finished.
He said that he was busy.
She told me that she would return.

entries.title: Reported questions
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Reported questionda gap tartibi xabar gapnikidek, yes/no uchun if/whether.
entries.explanationEn: Reported questions use statement order; yes/no questions are commonly introduced by if or whether.
entries.pattern: asked where S V; asked if S V
entries.tipUz: “Asked where was I” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: She asked whether I was ready.
He asked where I lived.
They asked if we had finished.

entries.title: Reported commands/requests
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Tell/ask/order + object + to V; inkorda not to V.
entries.explanationEn: Reported requests and commands commonly use ask/tell plus an object and an infinitive, with not before to for negatives.
entries.pattern: asked me to wait; told me not to worry
entries.tipUz: “He suggested me to leave” emas: “suggested that I leave / suggested leaving”.

examples.en: He told us to leave.
She asked me to wait.
He told us not to worry.

entries.title: Reporting verbs: gerund/infinitive
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Admit doing, deny doing, promise to do, advise somebody to do kabi boshqaruvlarni fe’l bilan o‘rganing.
entries.explanationEn: Reporting verbs select particular complement patterns; learn the verb and its construction together.
entries.pattern: deny + -ing; warn + object + to V
entries.tipUz: “Deny to take” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: She denied taking the money.
He admitted making a mistake.
She promised to help.

entries.title: Third conditional
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishda sodir bo‘lmagan ishning faraziy natijasi.
entries.explanationEn: A third conditional imagines a past condition and a past consequence that did not occur in that way.
entries.pattern: If + had V3, would have V3
entries.tipUz: If-qismida odatiy “would have” ishlatilmaydi.

examples.en: If I'd known, I'd have helped.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
If she had called, I would have answered.
examples.uz: U qo‘ng‘iroq qilganida javob bergan bo‘lardim.

entries.title: Mixed conditionals
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmish sharti→hozir natija yoki hozirgi holat→o‘tmish natija.
entries.explanationEn: Mixed conditionals combine different time references; the condition and result must remain logically compatible.
entries.pattern: If I had slept, I would feel better now
entries.tipUz: Vaqtlar mantiqiy mos kelishi shart.

examples.en: If I'd studied harder, I'd be more confident now.
If I had slept, I would feel better now.
examples.uz: Uxlaganimda hozir o‘zimni yaxshiroq his qilardim.

examples.en: If he were more careful, he would not have lost it.
examples.uz: U ehtiyotkorroq bo‘lganida uni yo‘qotmagan bo‘lardi.

entries.title: Unless/as long as/provided that
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Unless=agar ...masa, provided/as long as shart bajarilishini ta’kidlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Unless commonly means if not, while provided that/as long as emphasise a required condition; check the actual logical meaning.
entries.pattern: unless + affirmative clause
entries.tipUz: “Unless you don't...” ko‘pincha nojo‘ya double negative.

examples.en: We can go provided that it doesn't rain.
We will leave unless it rains.
You can stay as long as you keep quiet.

entries.title: Wish: present/past
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Hozirgi afsus uchun wish + past; o‘tmish afsusi uchun wish + past perfect.
entries.explanationEn: Wish plus a past form can express present unreality; wish plus past perfect commonly expresses past regret.
entries.pattern: I wish I knew; I wish I had known
entries.tipUz: “I wish I know” standart faraziy wish emas.

examples.en: I wish I spoke French.
I wish I had more time.
She wishes she had studied harder.

entries.title: Wish/if only + would
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Boshqa odam/holat o‘zgarishini istash yoki bezovtalik, ko‘pincha o‘z ixtiyoridagi oddiy niyat emas.
entries.explanationEn: Wish/if only plus would often requests a change or expresses annoyance; it is not a general substitute for every wish.
entries.pattern: I wish you would listen
entries.tipUz: “I wish I would be taller” odatda mos emas.

examples.en: If only the neighbours would be quiet!
I wish you would listen.
If only the bus would arrive!

entries.title: Non-defining relative clauses
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Qo‘shimcha izoh vergul bilan ajratiladi; that ishlatilmaydi; relative pronounni tashlab bo‘lmaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Non-defining relatives add supplementary information with commas; they do not take that or omit their relative pronoun.
entries.pattern: My aunt, who lives in Tashkent, ...
entries.tipUz: Vergul mazmunni o‘zgartiradi.

examples.en: My brother, who is a doctor, lives abroad.
My aunt, who lives nearby, called.
The bridge, which opened last year, is busy.
examples.uz: O‘tgan yili ochilgan ko‘prikda qatnov ko‘p.

entries.title: Where/when/whose relatives
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Joy, vaqt va egalikni bog‘laydi; whose narsalar uchun ham mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Where, when and whose express place, time and possession relationships; whose can also refer to things.
entries.pattern: the place where; the day when; the company whose profits ...
entries.tipUz: “Whose”ni faqat odamlar uchun deb o‘ylamang.

examples.en: I met a writer whose books I love.
examples.uz: Kitoblarini sevib o‘qiydigan yozuvchi bilan uchrashdim.

examples.en: This is the house where I grew up.
We visited a company whose products are exported.

entries.title: Relative prepositions
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Rasmiy uslubda preposition + whom/which; oddiy uslubda predlog oxirida ham bo‘lishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: A relative preposition can be stranded at the end or fronted with whom/which in a more formal pattern.
entries.pattern: the person to whom I spoke / the person I spoke to
entries.tipUz: “To that” preposition-frontingda relative that bilan ishlatilmaydi.

examples.en: This is the topic we talked about.
The woman I spoke to was helpful.
The woman to whom I spoke was helpful.
examples.uz: Men murojaat qilgan ayol yordam berdi; bu rasmiyroq shakl.

entries.title: Noun clauses: that/if/whether
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Butun gap ot vazifasida subject, object yoki complement bo‘lishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: A content clause can function as subject, object or complement; whether is generally preferred to if in a subject question-clause.
entries.pattern: I believe (that) ...; Whether ... matters
entries.tipUz: “If he agrees is unclear” subject-clause uchun odatda noqulay; whether afzal.

examples.en: Whether he agrees is unclear.
I believe that she is right.
Whether we can finish depends on the weather.

entries.title: Adverbial clauses: time/reason
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: When/while/before/after/since/as/because gaplar vaqt yoki sababni aniqlashtiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Adverbial clauses express relations such as time and reason; a word such as since can have more than one interpretation.
entries.pattern: Because S V, S V
entries.tipUz: Since sabab ham vaqt ham bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: Since it was late, we left.
While I cooked, she read.
Because the road was closed, we waited.

entries.title: Although/even though/whereas
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Although/even though kutilmagan zidlik, whereas ikki holatni qiyosiy zidlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Although/even though typically introduce concession, whereas contrasts situations; do not mechanically add but to the same link.
entries.pattern: Although S V, S V
entries.tipUz: “Although ..., but ...” bitta bog‘lanishda ortiqcha.

examples.en: Although it was expensive, we bought it.
Even though she was tired, she continued.
examples.uz: Charchagan bo‘lsa ham u davom etdi.

examples.en: I prefer tea, whereas he prefers coffee.
examples.uz: Men choyni ma’qul ko‘raman, u esa qahvani.

entries.title: Despite/in spite of
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Bular predlog: ortidan ot yoki -ing keladi; although esa clause oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Despite and in spite of are prepositions taking nouns or -ing forms, unlike although which introduces a clause.
entries.pattern: despite + noun/-ing; although + S V
entries.tipUz: “Despite it rained” noto‘g‘ri; “despite the fact that it rained” mumkin.

examples.en: Despite the rain, we played.
In spite of feeling tired, he worked.
Despite the delay, we arrived on time.

entries.title: Purpose clauses
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: To/in order to/so as to + V; so that + S + modal/verb.
entries.explanationEn: Infinitival purpose and finite so that clauses have different structures, especially when subjects differ.
entries.pattern: in order to save; so that we could save
entries.tipUz: “For to study” odatda emas.

examples.en: We left early so that we could catch the bus.
I called to ask a question.
She spoke slowly so that we could understand.
examples.uz: Biz tushunishimiz uchun u sekin gapirdi.

entries.title: Result clauses
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: So + adj/adv + that va such + (a/an) + adj + noun + that.
entries.explanationEn: Result constructions combine so with an adjective/adverb or such with a noun phrase, followed by that.
entries.pattern: so tired that; such a noise that
entries.tipUz: “Such tired” emas, “so tired”.

examples.en: It was so loud that we left.
She was so tired that she fell asleep.
examples.uz: U shu qadar charchagan ediki, uxlab qoldi.

examples.en: It was such a long journey that we needed a break.
examples.uz: Safar shunchalik uzoq ediki, tanaffus qilishimiz kerak bo‘ldi.

entries.title: Causative have/get
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Boshqa odam biror ishni siz uchun bajarganida have/get + object + V3.
entries.explanationEn: Have/get plus object and past participle can describe arranging for another person to do a service.
entries.pattern: have my hair cut; get my phone repaired
entries.tipUz: “I repaired my laptop” o‘zingiz qilganingizni anglatishi mumkin.

examples.en: I had my laptop repaired.
She had her hair cut.
We got the windows cleaned.

entries.title: Verb + object + infinitive
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Want/expect/allow/encourage somebody to do; make/let somebody do.
entries.explanationEn: The governing verb determines whether an object is followed by a to-infinitive or a bare infinitive.
entries.pattern: want him to go; let him go
entries.tipUz: “Let him to go” emas, “let him go”.

examples.en: They encouraged us to apply.
I want you to stay.
They let us enter.

entries.title: Verb + object + -ing
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: See/hear/watch + object + -ing jarayonning bir qismini; bare infinitive esa butun hodisani ta’kidlashi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: After perception verbs, -ing can foreground part of a process while a bare infinitive can present an event as a whole.
entries.pattern: saw him crossing / saw him cross
entries.tipUz: Farq ko‘pincha nuqtayi nazarda, faqat vaqt emas.

examples.en: I heard someone singing.
I saw her crossing the road.
I saw her cross the road.

entries.title: Verbal agreement advanced basics
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Each/every/everyone singular; a number of plural, the number of singular; there is/are keyingi otga moslashadi.
entries.explanationEn: Agreement follows the grammatical head and construction, not simply the nearest plural noun.
entries.pattern: Everyone is; a number of people are
entries.tipUz: “The number ... are” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: The number of applicants is rising.
Everyone is ready.
A number of students are absent.

entries.title: Quantifiers: few/a few/little/a little
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: A few/a little ijobiy “oz bo‘lsa-da bor”; few/little yetarli emasligini urg‘ulaydi.
entries.explanationEn: A few/a little present a small amount positively; few/little often imply less than wanted, with count/mass distinctions.
entries.pattern: few friends vs a few friends
entries.tipUz: “A little people” emas, “a few people”.

examples.en: We have a little time left.
I have a few friends here.
examples.uz: Bu yerda bir nechta do‘stim bor.

examples.en: There is little hope.

entries.title: Phrasal verbs grammar
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Verb+particle ba’zan ajraladi: pick it up; boshqalari ajralmaydi: look after it.
entries.explanationEn: Some phrasal verbs allow separation and place a pronoun between verb and particle; others do not separate.
entries.pattern: pick up the book / pick the book up / pick it up
entries.tipUz: “Turn off it” ajraladigan fe’lda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Please turn it off.
Please pick it up.
She looks after her brother.

entries.title: Verb–preposition patterns
entries.chapter: 04  B1  |  Murakkab gapga o‘tish
entries.explanationUz: Depend on, insist on, succeed in, apologise for kabi collocationlar ma’nosi bilan birga boshqaruvni ham belgilaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Verbs have conventional preposition and complement patterns, which should be learned with their meanings.
entries.pattern: depend on + noun; insist on + -ing
entries.tipUz: “Depend of” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: He insisted on paying.
We depend on public transport.
She succeeded in finding a solution.

entries.title: Aspect: habitual vs progressive
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Simple odat/fakt/holatga, progressive vaqtinchalik yoki rivojlanishdagi jarayonga mos; always + progressive ba’zan shikoyat.
entries.explanationEn: The simple/progressive contrast concerns aspect and viewpoint; always plus progressive can also convey a speaker's attitude.
entries.pattern: He always loses / He's always losing
entries.tipUz: Progressive harakatni qanchalik vaqtinchalik ko‘rsatishi kontekstga bog‘liq.

examples.en: Prices are rising rapidly.
He always leaves early.
He is always leaving his keys behind!

entries.title: Stative fe’llarning dynamic ishlatilishi
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Think, have, see, taste, feel ayrim ma’noda holat, ayrimida faol jarayon bo‘ladi.
entries.explanationEn: Some verbs have state and activity senses; progressive suitability follows the intended sense, not only the verb spelling.
entries.pattern: I think it's true / I'm thinking about it
entries.tipUz: “I'm knowing” odatda mumkin emas, “I'm thinking” mumkin.

examples.en: She's having lunch.
I think the plan is useful.
I am thinking about the plan.

entries.title: Perfect tense nuance
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Present perfectni tugagan davr bilan bog‘lashga ehtiyot bo‘ling; today/this week kabi davrlar hali ochiq bo‘lsa ishlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: A perfect construction can relate events to an unfinished current time period; a finished reference point changes the choice.
entries.pattern: I have met three clients today
entries.tipUz: O‘tib ketgan morning uchun past simple tabiiyroq.

examples.en: I've read two articles this morning.
examples.uz: Bugun ertalab ikki maqola o‘qidim (ertalab hali tugamagan bo‘lishi mumkin).

examples.en: I have answered three emails today.
examples.uz: Bugun uchta xatga javob berdim; bugungi davr hali davom etyapti.

examples.en: I answered three emails yesterday.

entries.title: Would for past habits
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Takrorlangan o‘tmish harakatlari uchun would; uzoq davom etgan state uchun used to ko‘proq.
entries.explanationEn: Habitual would commonly presents repeated past actions, while used to also readily describes former states.
entries.pattern: Every summer we'd visit ...
entries.tipUz: “Would be shy” odatda oldingi state uchun used to be kabi emas.

examples.en: My grandfather would tell us stories.
Every evening, she would read to us.
examples.uz: Har oqshom u bizga kitob o‘qib berardi.

examples.en: He used to be shy.

entries.title: Be to / be due to / be about to
aliases: Be to / be due to / be about to
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Rasmiy reja, kutilayotgan jadval va hozir boshlanish arafasidagi hodisani farqlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Be to, be due to and be about to differ in formality, scheduling and imminence.
entries.pattern: is to meet; is due to arrive; is about to start
entries.tipUz: “Due to” sabab predlogi ham bo‘ladi; kontekstni ajrating.

examples.en: The meeting is due to begin at nine.
The train is due to arrive at ten.
The show is about to begin.

entries.title: Future probability and certainty
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Will, be bound to, be likely to, be unlikely to, may/might ma’noda turli ishonch darajasi beradi.
entries.explanationEn: Future probability expressions indicate different degrees of commitment, but no modal has a fixed universal percentage.
entries.pattern: be likely to + V; be bound to + V
entries.tipUz: “Will” har doim 100% ishonch degani emas.

examples.en: Demand is likely to grow.
The plan is likely to succeed.
It might rain later.

entries.title: Modal deduction: present
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Must kuchli xulosa, can't/couldn't imkonsiz xulosa, may/might/could imkon.
entries.explanationEn: Epistemic must draws a strong conclusion; can't commonly expresses a strong negative deduction rather than prohibition.
entries.pattern: must be; can't be; might be
entries.tipUz: “Mustn't be home” xulosa emas, taqiq bo‘lishi mumkin; “can't be home” ishlating.

examples.en: She must be exhausted.
They must be at home; the lights are on.
examples.uz: Chiroqlar yoniq, ular uyda bo‘lsa kerak.

examples.en: That cannot be the right address.
examples.uz: Bu to‘g‘ri manzil bo‘lishi mumkin emas.

entries.title: Modal deduction: past
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Must/might/could/can't + have + V3 o‘tmishdagi voqea haqida xulosa.
entries.explanationEn: A modal plus have and a past participle makes a deduction about an earlier situation.
entries.pattern: must have left; might have missed
entries.tipUz: “Must had forgotten” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: He must have forgotten.
She might have missed the bus.
They cannot have finished already.
examples.uz: Ular allaqachon tugatgan bo‘lishi mumkin emas.

entries.title: Should have/needn't have
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Should have + V3=afsus/tanqid; needn't have + V3=ishni qildingiz, ammo shart emas edi.
entries.explanationEn: Needn't have commonly implies an action occurred unnecessarily; didn't need to alone does not establish whether it occurred.
entries.pattern: should have called; needn't have paid
entries.tipUz: “Didn't need to buy” ish bajarilmaganini majburiy bildirmaydi.

examples.en: You needn't have bought food.
examples.uz: Ovqat sotib olishingiz shart emas edi (ammo oldingiz).

examples.en: You should have called earlier.
I need not have hurried.
examples.uz: Shoshilishim shart emas ekan; ammo shoshildim.

entries.title: Could have / would have
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Could have o‘tmishda imkon; would have shartli yoki taxminiy natija; ma’no konteksga bog‘liq.
entries.explanationEn: Could have can express past possibility or opportunity; would have commonly depends on a condition or inferred outcome.
entries.pattern: could have won; would have won if...
entries.tipUz: “Could of” yozuvda xato; “could have”.

examples.en: We could have taken the train.
She could have won.
I would have helped if you had asked.

entries.title: Modal continuous/perfect continuous
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Must be doing / may have been doing kabi shakllar modal kuchi va aspectni birlashtiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Modal, perfect and progressive auxiliaries combine in a fixed order, each adding its own meaning.
entries.pattern: may be working; must have been sleeping
entries.tipUz: Modal + have been + -ing tartibini buzmaslik kerak.

examples.en: She may have been waiting outside.
examples.uz: U tashqarida kutayotgan bo‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: He must be sleeping.
They might have been working late.
examples.uz: Ular kechgacha ishlayotgan bo‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkin.

entries.title: The passive with two objects
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Give/show/offer kabi fe’llarda ikki xil passive ega bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin barcha fe’llarda emas.
entries.explanationEn: Some double-object verbs support passives focused on either recipient or thing; the pattern is not available for every verb.
entries.pattern: She was given a prize / A prize was given to her
entries.tipUz: “Explained me” emas, “explained it to me”.

examples.en: I was offered a job.
She was given a certificate.
A certificate was given to her.

entries.title: Reporting passive
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: It is said that... / He is believed to... rasmiy neytral hisobot tili.
entries.explanationEn: Reporting passives attribute a proposition or expectation; the wording does not itself establish that the proposition is true.
entries.pattern: It is claimed that S V; S + is thought to + V
entries.tipUz: It is believed that ni asossiz faktdek ko‘rsatish uchun ishlatmang.

examples.en: The policy is expected to change.
It is believed that the bridge is safe.
examples.uz: Ko‘prik xavfsiz deb hisoblanadi; bu qarash bildirilyapti.

examples.en: The bridge is believed to be safe.

entries.title: Have/get something done: unfortunate events
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Causative ba’zan kutilmagan salbiy voqeani ham bildiradi, xizmat ko‘rsatishni emas.
entries.explanationEn: Have plus object and participle can describe an adverse experience, not a service the subject requested.
entries.pattern: had my wallet stolen
entries.tipUz: Bu yerda u o‘g‘irlatishni buyurtma qilmagan.

examples.en: She had her phone stolen.
He had his bicycle stolen.
We had our windows broken.

entries.title: Infinitive forms
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Simple/perfect/progressive/passive infinitivlar vaqt va nisbatni bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Infinitives can mark progressive, perfect and passive relationships; select the form that fits the governing expression and timing.
entries.pattern: to do; to be doing; to have done; to be done
entries.tipUz: “Appears having left” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: He appears to have left.
She seems to be waiting.
The work needs to be checked.

entries.title: Gerund forms
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Doing, having done, being done, having been done turli jihatni ta’kidlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Gerund constructions can also carry perfect or passive meaning; extra auxiliaries need a reason in the context.
entries.pattern: having completed; being seen
entries.tipUz: Perfect gerund vaqt farqi aniq bo‘lgandagina kerak.

examples.en: She denied having seen the email.
He dislikes being interrupted.
She regretted having left early.

entries.title: Meaning-change verb patterns
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Remember to do/doing, stop to do/doing, try to do/doing, regret to say/doing kabi juftlar semantik jihatdan farq qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: A change between -ing and to-infinitive can change meaning after verbs such as remember, stop and try.
entries.pattern: remember to lock vs remember locking
entries.tipUz: “I stopped to smoke”=chekish uchun to‘xtadim.

examples.en: I stopped smoking.
Remember to lock the door.
I remember locking the door.

entries.title: Bare infinitive and help
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Modallardan, let/make va ba’zi perception fe’llardan keyin bare infinitive; passive make + to V.
entries.explanationEn: Bare infinitives follow certain modals and causative/perception verbs; passive made uses a to-infinitive.
entries.pattern: made him work / he was made to work
entries.tipUz: “Let me to leave” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: They let me leave early.
examples.uz: Ular menga erta ketishga ruxsat berdi.

examples.en: The teacher made us repeat the sentence.
We were made to repeat it.

entries.title: Participial adjectives
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Bored/boring kabi -ed his/ta’sirlangan odam, -ing ta’sir manbasi uchun ishlatiladi, lekin hammasi bunday emas.
entries.explanationEn: Participial adjectives can distinguish a source of an effect from the person experiencing it, but the distinction is not universal for every -ed/-ing word.
entries.pattern: interested / interesting
entries.tipUz: “I'm interesting in history” emas, “interested in history”.

examples.en: I was fascinated by the lecture.
The lesson was interesting.
We were interested in the lesson.

entries.title: Reduced defining relative
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Relative subject + be ma’lum holatda qisqarishi yoki active -ing/passive V3 participle clausega aylanishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: A reduced relative must preserve the noun's intended role and the time/voice relationship of the fuller clause.
entries.pattern: students studying abroad; data collected in 2024
entries.tipUz: Ma’no va subject mosligini tekshiring.

examples.en: The people living nearby complained.
The students waiting outside are ready.
The letters sent yesterday have arrived.

entries.title: Relative clauses after quantifiers
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Some of whom/most of which/none of whose kabi bog‘lanish formal murakkab jumlalarni beradi.
entries.explanationEn: Quantified supplementary relatives use forms such as some of whom and most of which, with an appropriate antecedent.
entries.pattern: ten students, three of whom ...
entries.tipUz: “Most of who” emas, “most of whom”.

examples.en: We interviewed 20 people, most of whom agreed.
examples.uz: 20 kishidan intervyu oldik, ularning aksariyati rozi bo‘ldi.

examples.en: We met five students, two of whom spoke Uzbek.
examples.uz: Besh talaba bilan uchrashdik, ularning ikkitasi o‘zbekcha gapirdi.

examples.en: She bought three books, all of which were useful.
examples.uz: U uchta kitob oldi, ularning hammasi foydali edi.

entries.title: Preposition + wh- relative
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: In which, for whom, to whom rasmiy; where va oxirgi preposition oddiyroq.
entries.explanationEn: Fronting a relative preposition commonly makes the expression more formal; it is a register choice rather than automatic improvement.
entries.pattern: the method by which; a person to whom
entries.tipUz: Formallik yaxshi, ammo sun’iy ko‘paytirish shart emas.

examples.en: This is the basis on which we proceed.
This is the room in which we worked.
She is the person on whom we rely.

entries.title: Non-finite time/reason clauses
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: After doing, before leaving, while waiting kabi qisqartmalar bitta subjectda tabiiy.
entries.explanationEn: An understood subject in a reduced time/reason clause normally needs to match the main-clause subject.
entries.pattern: After + -ing, S + V
entries.tipUz: Dangling modifierga ehtiyot bo‘ling: “Walking home, the rain started” mantiqsiz.

examples.en: After reviewing the data, we revised the plan.
examples.uz: Ma’lumotni ko‘rib chiqib rejani qayta tuzdik.

examples.en: Before leaving, I checked the door.
While waiting, she read a book.

entries.title: Participle clauses: cause/result
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Having V3 avvalgi ishni, V-ing bir vaqtlik/sabab/natijani; ko‘pincha formal uslub.
entries.explanationEn: A participle clause can express a prior action, cause or result; an unexpressed subject must be interpreted consistently.
entries.pattern: Having finished the report, she left
entries.tipUz: Subject tushib qolsa, ikki clause egasi bir xil bo‘lishi kerak.

examples.en: Having checked the figures, we submitted the report.
Having finished the work, he went home.
The road flooded, causing delays.
examples.uz: Yo‘lni suv bosib, kechikishlarga sabab bo‘ldi.

entries.title: Concessive clauses
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Though, even though, even if, while, much as turli zidlik va farazlarni ifodalaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Concession and hypothetical concession differ: even though presents a fact, while even if can present an imagined possibility.
entries.pattern: even if (hypothetical); even though (fact)
entries.tipUz: Even if va even though bir xil emas.

examples.en: Even if it rains, we'll go.
Even though it was cold, we walked.
Even if it gets cold, we will walk.
examples.uz: Sovuq bo‘lib qolsa ham piyoda yuramiz.

entries.title: As if / as though
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Ko‘rinish, taxmin yoki noreal vaziyat: as if + present/past/perfect; past irrealisni ko‘rsatishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: As if/as though can describe appearances or hypothetical comparison; past forms are not obligatory in every use.
entries.pattern: as if he knew; as if he had seen
entries.tipUz: Har bir as if dan keyin past ishlatilishi shart emas.

examples.en: He talks as if he knew everything.
She looks as if she is tired.
He spends as though he were rich.
examples.uz: U o‘zini boydek tutib pul sarflaydi.

entries.title: Suppose / supposing / what if
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Farazni kiritadigan bog‘lovchi ifodalar; real yoki noreal zamon uyg‘unligi tanlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Suppose, supposing and what if introduce hypothetical situations whose forms depend on the intended remoteness and time.
entries.pattern: Suppose + past ...?
entries.tipUz: “What if ...?” ko‘pincha mustaqil faraz savoli.

examples.en: What if the plan fails?
Suppose we missed the train. What would we do?
examples.uz: Poyezdga ulgurmay qoldik deylik. Nima qilardik?

examples.en: What if she does not agree?

entries.title: Adverb position and scope
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Only, almost, even, just kabi fokus ravishlari qaysi bo‘lakni o‘zgartirayotganiga qarab ma’noni o‘zgartiradi.
entries.explanationEn: The position of a focus adverb can change which part of a proposition is restricted or emphasised.
entries.pattern: Only she spoke / She only spoke
entries.tipUz: “Only” joylashuvi noaniqlik tug‘dirishi mumkin.

examples.en: I only asked a question.
Only Ali answered.
Ali answered only one question.
examples.uz: Ali faqat bitta savolga javob berdi.

entries.title: Degree and gradability
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Absolute va gradable sifatlar: very big; absolutely impossible; nearly full. Kuchaytirgichlar har doim almashtirilmaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Choose degree modifiers compatible with the adjective and intended meaning; usage is more flexible than an absolute two-list rule.
entries.pattern: highly likely; utterly ridiculous
entries.tipUz: “Very impossible” o‘rniga “virtually impossible” tabiiyroq.

examples.en: The outcome is highly unlikely.
The room is very large.
The bottle is almost empty.

entries.title: Determiner stacking/order
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Predeterminer (all/both/half) + central (the/my) + postdeterminer (three/next) + noun.
entries.explanationEn: Determiners have ordering constraints; an article and possessive cannot ordinarily both occupy the same central slot.
entries.pattern: all three of my books; the first two chapters
entries.tipUz: “The my book” bitta otda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Both these solutions work.
All these books are useful.
The first two lessons are short.

entries.title: Articles with generic reference
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: “A tiger is...”, “The tiger is...”, “Tigers are...” uchalasi umumlashtirishga xizmat qilishi mumkin, uslub va fokus farqli.
