entries.explanationEn: Generic reference can use plural, mass or appropriate singular expressions; article choice changes interpretation and register.
entries.pattern: Tigers are mammals
entries.tipUz: “The education” abstrakt umumiy ma’noda odatda ortiqcha.

examples.en: Education benefits society.
Dogs need exercise.
A whale is a mammal.

entries.title: Mass vs count shifts
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Experience, paper, coffee, work, room kabi otlar kontekstga qarab count/mass bo‘ladi.
entries.explanationEn: A noun can shift between count and mass senses, changing its article, plural and interpretation.
entries.pattern: experience / an experience; coffee / two coffees
entries.tipUz: “Many experiences” voqealar, “much experience” tajriba.

examples.en: I had an unusual experience.
She has a lot of experience.
We ordered two coffees.

entries.title: Complex noun phrases
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Pre-/post-modification yordamida akademik ma’lumotni ixcham berish mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: A noun phrase can include premodifiers and postmodifiers, but excessive compression can hide relationships.
entries.pattern: the recent sharp rise in demand for housing
entries.tipUz: O‘ta uzun noun phrase o‘qishni qiyinlashtiradi.

examples.en: The rapid expansion of public transport has benefits.
examples.uz: Jamoat transportining tez kengayishi foyda beradi.

examples.en: The recent rise in prices worries us.
The report on local transport is ready.

entries.title: Academic nominalisation
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Fe’l/sifatdan ot yasab mazmunni mavhumlashtiradi, lekin agentni yashirishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Nominalisation packages an action or property as a noun; keep the actor and relationship clear where they matter.
entries.pattern: fail→failure; efficient→efficiency
entries.tipUz: “The implementation of the improvement...” kabi ortiqcha otlashtirishdan saqlaning.

examples.en: The expansion of services improved access.
The team improved the service.
The improvement of the service took a year.
examples.uz: Xizmatni yaxshilash bir yil davom etdi.

entries.title: Parallel structures
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: And/or/nor bilan bog‘langan qismlar grammatik shakli mos bo‘lsa gap ravon.
entries.explanationEn: Parallel structures coordinate comparable grammatical forms, helping readers see the intended relationship.
entries.pattern: to plan, to build and to test
entries.tipUz: “To reduce ... and improving ...” parallel emas.

examples.en: The scheme aims to reduce costs and improve quality.
examples.uz: Reja xarajatni kamaytirish va sifatni oshirishga qaratilgan.

examples.en: She enjoys reading and writing.
We aim to listen carefully and respond clearly.
examples.uz: Diqqat bilan tinglash va aniq javob berishni maqsad qilganmiz.

entries.title: Correlative conjunctions
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Not only ... but also; either ... or; neither ... nor; both ... and konstruktsiyalari simmetrik bo‘lishi lozim.
entries.explanationEn: Correlative constructions should connect elements in matching structural positions, with agreement checked separately.
entries.pattern: not only A but also B
entries.tipUz: Ko‘makchi va zamon parallel saqlansin.

examples.en: The policy is both practical and affordable.
She is both patient and practical.
examples.uz: U sabrli ham, amaliy fikrlaydigan ham.

examples.en: We can either walk or take a bus.
examples.uz: Piyoda yurishimiz yoki avtobusga chiqishimiz mumkin.

entries.title: Subject–verb agreement: distance
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Ega bilan fe’l orasida uzun aniqlovchi bo‘lsa, fe’l yaqin otga emas, asosiy head nounga moslashadi.
entries.explanationEn: A long modifier between subject and verb does not normally change the head noun's agreement.
entries.pattern: The quality of the services is ...
entries.tipUz: “The quality ... are” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: The results of the survey are clear.
The colour of the walls is unusual.
The students in the next room are waiting.

entries.title: Collective nouns and varieties
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Team/government/staff ayrim British English kontekstlarida plural agreement oladi, American Englishda singular ko‘proq.
entries.explanationEn: Collective-noun agreement varies with variety and whether the group is presented as a unit or as members; maintain a coherent choice.
entries.pattern: The team is / The team are (BrE)
entries.tipUz: Dialektga qarab tabiiylik o‘zgaradi.

examples.en: The committee has reached a decision.
The team is preparing its report.
examples.uz: Jamoa o‘z hisobotini tayyorlayapti; yaxlit birlik nazarda tutilgan.

examples.en: The team are arguing among themselves.
examples.uz: Jamoa a’zolari o‘zaro bahslashyapti; bu Britancha a’zolarga qaratilgan shakl.

entries.title: Negation scope
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Not all va none, not necessarily va necessarily not bir xil emas.
entries.explanationEn: Negation has scope: not all denies universality, while none denies every member of the relevant set.
entries.pattern: Not all students passed ≠ No students passed
entries.tipUz: “Not everyone” hech kim emas degani emas.

examples.en: Not everyone agreed.
Not all the doors are open.
None of the doors is open.

entries.title: Discourse reference
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: This/that/these/those/such/one/ones/so/do so oldingi g‘oyaga qaytib bog‘liqlikni saqlaydi.
entries.explanationEn: A reference expression should lead the reader back to a clear earlier entity or proposition.
entries.pattern: This suggests ...; those who ...
entries.tipUz: “This” referenti aniq bo‘lishi lozim.

examples.en: This suggests that the policy needs revision.
examples.uz: Bu siyosat qayta ko‘rilishi kerakligini ko‘rsatadi.

examples.en: The road was closed. This caused delays.
examples.uz: Yo‘l yopiq edi. Bu kechikishlarga sabab bo‘ldi.

examples.en: I need new shoes. These are worn out.
examples.uz: Yangi tufli kerak. Bular eskirib ketgan.

entries.title: Punctuation: subordinate clauses
entries.chapter: 05  B2  |  Aniqlik, argument va murakkab sintaksis
entries.explanationUz: Oldinga chiqqan adverbial clause ko‘pincha vergul bilan ajratiladi; defining relative esa vergulsiz.
entries.explanationEn: Punctuation reflects clause relationships; fronted adverbials and defining relatives have different conventions.
entries.pattern: If it rains, we'll stay / We'll stay if it rains
entries.tipUz: Vergul o‘rnini meaning va readability asosida tanlang.

examples.en: When the price falls, demand often rises.
If you finish early, call me.
The book that I borrowed is useful.
examples.uz: Olib turgan kitobim foydali; aniqlovchi qism vergulsiz.

entries.title: Negative inversion: never/rarely
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Salbiy yoki cheklovchi oldingi ravishlardan keyin auxiliary + subject inversiyasi talab qilinadi.
entries.explanationEn: Fronted negative or restrictive adverbials can trigger auxiliary-subject inversion in a formal clause.
entries.pattern: Never/Rarely + aux + S + V
entries.tipUz: “Rarely I have seen” formal inversion qolipida noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Rarely have I seen such progress.
Never have I felt so relieved.
Rarely do we see such a clear result.

entries.title: Only after/only when inversion
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Only + adverbial boshida kelsa, inversiya asosiy clause’da, only-qismda emas.
entries.explanationEn: When only fronts an adverbial clause, inversion belongs in the main clause, not inside the only-clause.
entries.pattern: Only after X did S V
entries.tipUz: “Only after did we leave...” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Only then did I understand.
Only after she explained did I understand.
Only when the rain stopped did we leave.

entries.title: Not only ... but also + inversion
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Not only boshda kelsa birinchi clausal qismda inversion bo‘ladi.
entries.explanationEn: Clause-initial not only triggers inversion in its first clause; the second clause commonly keeps ordinary order.
entries.pattern: Not only + auxiliary + S + V, but S also ...
entries.tipUz: “Not only profits fell” boshiga qo‘yilgan formal qolip emas.

examples.en: Not only did profits fall, but costs also rose.
examples.uz: Foyda kamayibgina qolmay, xarajatlar ham oshdi.

examples.en: Not only did she help, but she also stayed late.
examples.uz: U yordam beribgina qolmay, kechgacha ham qoldi.

examples.en: Not only is it cheaper, but it is also safer.

entries.title: Hardly/Scarcely/No sooner
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Ketma-ket hodisalar: hardly/scarcely ... when; no sooner ... than, ko‘pincha past perfect inversion.
entries.explanationEn: The conventional links are hardly/scarcely…when and no sooner…than, often with past-perfect inversion.
entries.pattern: Hardly had S V3 when ...; No sooner had S V3 than ...
entries.tipUz: “No sooner ... when” odatda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: No sooner had we arrived than it began to rain.
Hardly had she sat down when the phone rang.
examples.uz: U endigina o‘tirgan edi, telefon jiringladi.

examples.en: Scarcely had we started when it rained.

entries.title: Under no circumstances / on no account
aliases: Under no circumstances / on no account
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Juda kuchli taqiqni formal urg‘ulaydi; asosiy clause inversiya oladi.
entries.explanationEn: A fronted negative restriction such as under no circumstances gives strong formal emphasis and triggers inversion.
entries.pattern: Under no circumstances + should + S + V
entries.tipUz: “Under no circumstances data should...” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Under no circumstances should data be altered.
examples.uz: Ma’lumot hech qanday holatda o‘zgartirilmasligi kerak.

examples.en: On no account should you share a password.
Under no circumstances must the exit be blocked.
examples.uz: Chiqish yo‘li hech qanday holatda to‘sib qo‘yilmasligi kerak.

entries.title: Conditional inversion: had
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: If tushirilgan o‘tmish shart gap: Had I known ...
entries.explanationEn: Had-subject inversion can replace if in a past counterfactual condition; the main clause retains its intended consequence.
entries.pattern: Had + S + V3, would have + V3
entries.tipUz: “Had I knew” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Had I known, I would have objected.
Had we left earlier, we would have arrived on time.
examples.uz: Oldinroq chiqqanimizda vaqtida yetib kelgan bo‘lardik.

examples.en: Had she asked, I would have helped.

entries.title: Conditional inversion: were
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Noreal hozir/kelajak sharti rasmiy ifodada Were + subject ...
entries.explanationEn: Were-subject inversion introduces a more formal hypothetical condition, including were…to patterns.
entries.pattern: Were + S + to V / adjective/noun
entries.tipUz: “Were I was...” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: Were I in your position, I would wait.
Were she here, she would explain.
Were the plan to fail, we would try again.
examples.uz: Reja amalga oshmay qolsa, qayta urinardik.

entries.title: Conditional inversion: should
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Kam ehtimolli, muloyim shart: should you need; rasmiy muloqotda qo‘llanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Should-subject inversion can present a contingent future condition, often in formal or polite instructions.
entries.pattern: Should + S + V, main clause
entries.tipUz: Bu oddiy “should=maslahat” ma’nosidan farq qiladi.

examples.en: Should you require assistance, contact us.
Should you need help, call me.
examples.uz: Yordam kerak bo‘lib qolsa, qo‘ng‘iroq qiling.

examples.en: Should the weather change, we will return.

entries.title: Cleft: it is/was ... that
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Muayyan bo‘lakni ajratib urg‘ulaydi; kim, qachon, nimani ko‘rsatish mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: An it-cleft highlights a chosen part of the message; the focus and remaining clause must fit each other.
entries.pattern: It + be + focus + that/who + clause
entries.tipUz: Har jumlada cleft ishlatish sun’iy.

examples.en: It was the methodology that raised concerns.
It was yesterday that she called.
It is the cost that worries me.

entries.title: Pseudo-cleft: what ... is
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Asosiy fikrni oxirga ko‘chiradi yoki oldingi clause bilan ajratadi.
entries.explanationEn: A pseudo-cleft organises a wh-clause and a focused complement, often placing the key information near the end.
entries.pattern: What + clause + be + focus
entries.tipUz: “What I need is to rest” va “What I need is rest” ikkalasi kontekstga mos.

examples.en: What matters most is consistency.
What I need is more time.
What surprised us was the result.

entries.title: All-cleft / the reason why
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Discourse fokusini boshqaradi; norasmiy va rasmiy variantlari farq qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: All-clefts and reason clauses organise focus; formal reason constructions commonly use is that rather than is because.
entries.pattern: All I want is ...; The reason ... is that ...
entries.tipUz: “The reason is because” nutqda uchrasa-da, rasmiyda “is that” afzal.

examples.en: The reason the trial failed was that the sample was too small.
examples.uz: Sinov muvaffaqiyatsizligining sababi namuna kichikligida edi.

examples.en: All I want is a clear answer.
The reason we waited was that the road was closed.

entries.title: Fronting for contrast
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Oldinga ko‘chirilgan object/adverbial eski-yangi ma’lumot va kontrastni boshqaradi.
entries.explanationEn: Fronting can establish contrast or topic without being an ordinary neutral word-order pattern.
entries.pattern: This part I understand; that part I don't
entries.tipUz: Har fronting grammatik xato emas, lekin nutq uslubiga mos bo‘lsin.

examples.en: This proposal I support; the alternative I reject.
examples.uz: Bu taklifni qo‘llayman, muqobilini rad etaman.

examples.en: This book I enjoyed; that one I did not.
examples.uz: Bu kitob menga yoqdi, anavisi esa yoqmadi.

examples.en: The first question I can answer.
examples.uz: Birinchi savolga javob bera olaman; urg‘u aynan birinchi savolda.

entries.title: Emphatic do/does/did
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Fe’l tasdiqini urg‘ulash uchun do-support ishlatiladi; imlo emas, kontekst muhim.
entries.explanationEn: Emphatic do/does/did carries agreement or past marking and is followed by the base verb.
entries.pattern: S + do/does/did + base verb
entries.tipUz: “I do appreciated” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: I do appreciate your help.
She does know the answer.
We did check the figures.

entries.title: So/neither inversion
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Oldingi fikrga qo‘shilish yoki o‘xshashlik: So + aux + S; Neither/Nor + aux + S.
entries.explanationEn: So/neither plus auxiliary and subject expresses parallel agreement; a non-inverted so-clause can have a different meaning.
entries.pattern: So do I; Neither has he
entries.tipUz: “So I can” bir xil ma’no emas; bu tasdiq bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: She can drive, and so can I.
He likes tea, and so do I.
She has not finished, and neither have I.

entries.title: Subjunctive: mandative
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Suggest/recommend/insist that + subject + base verb, ayniqsa American/formal English; British Englishda should varianti ham.
entries.explanationEn: Mandative subjunctives commonly use a base verb after a recommendation or requirement, including be for every person.
entries.pattern: recommend that he go / he should go
entries.tipUz: “He goes” American mandative qolipiga to‘g‘ri kelmaydi.

examples.en: They recommended that the rule be revised.
examples.uz: Ular qoidani qayta ko‘rishni tavsiya qildi.

examples.en: They insisted that he leave.
We recommend that the work be checked.

entries.title: Fixed subjunctive and wishes
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: If I were, God save ..., so be it, long live ... kabi qoliplar tarixiy subjunctive izlari.
entries.explanationEn: Some fixed expressions preserve subjunctive forms; irrealis were is widely used in formal hypothetical conditions.
entries.pattern: If I were you ...
entries.tipUz: “Was” nutqda uchraydi, rasmiy farazda were keng tarqalgan.

examples.en: If I were you, I'd reconsider.
examples.uz: Sizning o‘rningizda bo‘lsam qayta ko‘rib chiqardim.

examples.en: If she were here, she would help.
examples.uz: U shu yerda bo‘lsa, yordam berardi.

examples.en: Long live friendship!

entries.title: Would rather / it's time
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Would rather + past (boshqa odamga nisbatan faraz), it's (high) time + past; asl ma’no hozirgi/kelajak.
entries.explanationEn: A past form after would rather with another subject or after it is time can refer to present/future preference, not past events.
entries.pattern: I'd rather you didn't; It's time we left
entries.tipUz: “I'd rather you to tell me” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: I'd rather you told me directly.
I would rather you waited here.
It is time we went home.

entries.title: As if + perfect irrealis
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: O‘tmishdagi haqiqatga zid ko‘rinishni as if/as though + had V3 bilan berish.
entries.explanationEn: A perfect form after as if/as though can place the comparison before another reference point; counterfactuality depends on context.
entries.pattern: look as if + past perfect
entries.tipUz: Past perfect har doim yolg‘onlikni majburan anglatmaydi, kontekstga bog‘liq.

examples.en: He acted as if nothing had happened.
She looked as if she had seen a ghost.
He spoke as though he had known us for years.
examples.uz: U bizni yillardan beri taniydigandek gapirdi.

entries.title: Participle clauses: perfect/passive
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Having been V3 / V3 / being V3 bir bo‘lakni xos tarzda qisqartiradi; agent va vaqtga ehtiyot bo‘ling.
entries.explanationEn: Perfect and passive participle clauses combine prior timing with an affected subject; keep the understood participant consistent.
entries.pattern: Having been informed, S + V
entries.tipUz: Passive subject semantik jihatdan bir xil bo‘lishi zarur.

examples.en: Having been warned, the team changed its plan.
Having been invited, she attended.
Warned about the delay, we left early.

entries.title: Absolute constructions
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: “Weather permitting, ...”, “All things considered, ...” o‘z subjectiga ega non-finite construction.
entries.explanationEn: An absolute construction has its own expressed participant rather than sharing an omitted subject in the usual way.
entries.pattern: Noun + V-ing/V3, main clause
entries.tipUz: Bular barcha gaplarga qo‘shiladigan universal bezak emas.

examples.en: Weather permitting, we'll start at dawn.
The work finished, we went home.
All things considered, the plan worked well.
examples.uz: Barcha jihatlarni hisobga olganda reja yaxshi ishladi.

entries.title: Ellipsis after auxiliaries
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Takroriy verb phrase kontekstdan ravshan bo‘lsa tashlanadi: I can, I haven't, I would.
entries.explanationEn: Auxiliary ellipsis omits recoverable verb material while preserving an appropriate auxiliary, tense and polarity.
entries.pattern: I can (do it); she hasn't (done it)
entries.tipUz: Auxiliary agreement/tenses saqlanishi kerak.

examples.en: I haven't read it, but she has.
She can swim, but I cannot.
examples.uz: U suza oladi, men esa yo‘q.

examples.en: I thought he would help, and he did.
examples.uz: U yordam beradi deb o‘ylagandim, u shunday qildi.

entries.title: Ellipsis after to / gapping
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Want to, hope to; koordinatsiyada ikkinchi qismdagi fe’l tushirilishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: An infinitive marker can stand for an understood infinitival phrase, while gapping can omit repeated material in coordination.
entries.pattern: I wanted to (go); Ali chose tea, and Sara coffee
entries.tipUz: Ellipsis tushunarsizlik tug‘dirmasligi shart.

examples.en: I wanted to leave, but I couldn't.
I wanted to go, but she did not want to.
examples.uz: Men borishni xohladim, u esa xohlamadi.

examples.en: Ali ordered tea, and Lola coffee.
examples.uz: Ali choy buyurdi, Lola esa qahva.

entries.title: Substitution: one/ones/so/do so
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Oldingi ot/fe’l/entire clause o‘rnini bosadi; one count noun bilan keladi.
entries.explanationEn: One/ones, so and do so replace different kinds of prior expression; choose the substitute that fits its antecedent.
entries.pattern: the red one; I think so; did so
entries.tipUz: “The cheaper” ham kontekstda otlashishi mumkin; registrga qarang.

examples.en: She chose the cheaper one.
I prefer the blue ones.
He asked us to wait, and we did so.
examples.uz: U bizdan kutishni so‘radi, biz shunday qildik.

entries.title: Concession: much as / adjective as
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: “Much as I respect...”, “Tired as she was...” kuchli rasmiy zidlik ifodalaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Fronted adjective-as and much-as patterns express concession in a more literary/formal style.
entries.pattern: Adj + as + S + be, main clause
entries.tipUz: “As tired he was” odatiy concessive qolip emas.

examples.en: Tired as he was, he kept working.
Young as she is, she is very capable.
examples.uz: Yosh bo‘lsa ham, u juda qobiliyatli.

examples.en: Much as I respect him, I disagree.
examples.uz: Uni qanchalik hurmat qilsam ham, fikriga qo‘shilmayman.

entries.title: Inversion after so/such
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Natija gapida kuchaytirish uchun “So + adjective + be/aux + S + that ...” mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: So/such fronting can create a formal emphatic result construction with inversion; ordinary alternatives may be clearer in conversation.
entries.pattern: So + adj + was + S + that
entries.tipUz: Ko‘proq kitobiy; speakingda zarurat bo‘lmasa qo‘llamang.

examples.en: So severe was the storm that flights were cancelled.
examples.uz: Bo‘ron shu qadar kuchli ediki, reyslar bekor qilindi.

examples.en: So tired was she that she fell asleep.
examples.uz: U shu qadar charchagan ediki, uxlab qoldi.

examples.en: Such was the demand that we extended the course.
examples.uz: Talab shu darajada ediki, kursni uzaytirdik.

entries.title: Advanced comparisons
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: The more..., the more...; no more than; as ... as; not nearly as; far from.
entries.explanationEn: Comparative constructions express linked changes, ratios or limits; their logic must match the intended numerical relationship.
entries.pattern: The more S V, the more S V
entries.tipUz: “The more better” emas.

examples.en: The more carefully we plan, the fewer errors we make.
examples.uz: Qanchalik puxta rejalashtirsak, shunchalik kam xato qilamiz.

examples.en: The more I practise, the easier it gets.
examples.uz: Qancha ko‘p mashq qilsam, shuncha osonlashadi.

examples.en: This room is not nearly as large as that one.
examples.uz: Bu xona anavisidek katta emas, ancha kichik.

entries.title: Hedging: likelihood
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Seem/appear/tend/likely/may/suggest/possibly ehtimolni dalilga moslash; qat’iy xulosadan qoching.
entries.explanationEn: Hedging aligns the strength of a claim with the available evidence rather than removing the need for evidence.
entries.pattern: It appears that ...; may + V
entries.tipUz: Dalil bo‘lmasa “prove conclusively” deb yozmang.

examples.en: The findings suggest that demand may increase.
The results may indicate a change.
This approach seems useful.

entries.title: Attribution and reporting stance
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Claim/argue/maintain/acknowledge/concede/assert/contend ma’no va ishonch farqini beradi.
entries.explanationEn: Reporting verbs communicate the writer's stance towards another proposition; claim, acknowledge and argue are not neutral synonyms.
entries.pattern: X argues that...; Y acknowledges that...
entries.tipUz: “Claim” ba’zan shubha ohangini berishi mumkin.

examples.en: Researchers acknowledge that the sample was limited.
The author argues that costs matter.
The team acknowledged that the evidence was limited.

entries.title: Complex complement clauses
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: “The fact that...”, “the possibility of ...”, “it is likely that ...”, “be aware of ...” boshqaruvini ajrating.
entries.explanationEn: Nouns and adjectives select particular content-clause or prepositional complements; keep those patterns distinct.
entries.pattern: fact that + clause; possibility of + -ing
entries.tipUz: “The possibility to rising” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: There is a possibility that costs will rise.
The fact that she agreed surprised me.
We discussed the possibility of leaving early.

entries.title: Extraposition: dummy it
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Uzun subjectni oxirga ko‘chirish: It is important to..., It seems that...; it bu yerda haqiqiy referent emas.
entries.explanationEn: Dummy it can occupy the subject position while a heavier clause comes later; it need not refer to a real object.
entries.pattern: It + be + adjective + to V/that clause
entries.tipUz: “Is essential to...” mustaqil gapda ega yetishmaydi.

examples.en: It is essential that data remain accurate.
It is useful to compare examples.
It seems that they have left.

entries.title: Existential there advanced
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: There appears/seems/happens to be; there has been; there is likely to be.
entries.explanationEn: Existential there can combine with perfect forms and raising expressions such as seems to be.
entries.pattern: There + seems + to be + noun
entries.tipUz: “It appears a discrepancy” emas.

examples.en: There appears to be a discrepancy.
There has been a mistake.
There is likely to be a delay.

entries.title: Not until / not since inversion
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Vaqt cheklovi boshga chiqqanda asosiy clause inversiyasi.
entries.explanationEn: A fronted not-until/not-since restriction triggers inversion in the main clause, not in the subordinate time clause.
entries.pattern: Not until + clause + auxiliary + S + V
entries.tipUz: “Not until did we test...” inversiya joyi xato.

examples.en: Not until we tested it did we notice the flaw.
Not until she arrived did we start.
Not since I moved have I felt so relaxed.
examples.uz: Ko‘chib kelganimdan beri bunchalik xotirjam bo‘lmaganman.

entries.title: Contrastive focus and information flow
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Given/new info; topic/comment; end-focus/end-weight orqali o‘qilish osonlashadi.
entries.explanationEn: Information flow places topics, contrast and new information where the reader can follow them; heavier material often comes later.
entries.pattern: This report examines X; the most striking result is Y
entries.tipUz: Uzun subjectni har safar gap boshiga tiqmang.

examples.en: A major concern remains the lack of funding.
This method has one advantage: its speed.
examples.uz: Bu usulning bitta afzalligi bor: tezligi.

examples.en: What we need now is a practical solution.
examples.uz: Hozir bizga kerak bo‘lgani — amaliy yechim.

entries.title: Parenthetical clauses
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: “I believe”, “as you know”, “it seems” kiritmalari fikrga ehtiyotkorlik yoki muomala ohangi qo‘shadi.
entries.explanationEn: A parenthetical clause adds stance or interactional information without being the main proposition.
entries.pattern: This is, I think, the best option
entries.tipUz: Ortiqcha parenthetical ravonlikni buzadi.

examples.en: The scheme, I would argue, is sustainable.
This is, I believe, a useful change.
The result, as you know, was unexpected.

entries.title: Advanced comma control
entries.chapter: 06  C1  |  Murakkab grammatikani erkin boshqarish
entries.explanationUz: Non-defining appositive va parenthetical ko‘pincha vergul bilan, colon izoh bilan, semicolon yaqin mustaqil clause bilan ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Commas, colons and semicolons serve different structural purposes; a comma alone does not normally join two independent clauses.
entries.pattern: The results were mixed; further study is needed.
entries.tipUz: Comma splice: “It was costly, we stopped” xato.

examples.en: The pattern is clear: demand rises when prices fall.
examples.uz: Qolip aniq: narx tushsa, talab oshadi.

examples.en: The work was difficult; we continued.
We need one thing: more time.
examples.uz: Bizga bitta narsa kerak: ko‘proq vaqt.

entries.title: Deontic vs epistemic modality
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Must/should/may kontekstdan kelib chiqib vazifa-ruxsat yoki dalildan xulosa bildiradi; o‘xshash shakl turli ma’no.
entries.explanationEn: The same modal can express obligation/permission or an inference; interpretation depends on the proposition and context.
entries.pattern: You must leave / You must be tired
entries.tipUz: Deontic mustn’t (taqiq) va epistemic can’t (ishonmaslik)ni ajrating.

examples.en: The figures must be wrong.
You must wear a seat belt.
You must be tired after the journey.

entries.title: Modal remoteness
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Could/would/might nafaqat past, balki ehtiyotkorlik va masofaviy farazni beradi.
entries.explanationEn: Could, would and might can mark politeness or hypothetical distance rather than simply referring to past time.
entries.pattern: Could you...? / Would you mind...?
entries.tipUz: Oddiy past time deb o‘qimang.

examples.en: That might be worth considering.
examples.uz: Buni ko‘rib chiqish foydali bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: Could you explain that again?
I would prefer to wait.

entries.title: Counterfactual layering
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Would have been doing, could have had, might not have been kabi kengaygan modallar bir nechta vaqt/nisbat qatlamini birlashtiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Layered modal-perfect-progressive expressions combine several meanings; identify the modal, time relationship and aspect separately.
entries.pattern: modal + have + been + V-ing
entries.tipUz: Har qatlam ma’nosini alohida tekshiring.

examples.en: Without help, we might still have been waiting.
examples.uz: Yordamsiz hali ham kutayotgan bo‘lishimiz mumkin edi.

examples.en: She could have been waiting outside.
examples.uz: U tashqarida kutayotgan bo‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkin edi.

examples.en: If we had stayed, we would have been working all night.

entries.title: Pragmatic softeners
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: I was wondering if..., I don't suppose..., might possibly..., would you mind ...? xushmuomalalikni grammatika orqali bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Grammatical distance can soften a request, with past or modal forms referring to a present interaction.
entries.pattern: I was wondering whether + clause
entries.tipUz: Bu yerda past continuous o‘tmish harakatini majburan bildirmaydi.

examples.en: I was wondering if you had a moment.
examples.uz: Bir daqiqangiz bormikan, deb so‘ramoqchi edim.

examples.en: I was wondering whether you could help.
examples.uz: Yordam bera olarmikan deb so‘ramoqchi edim.

examples.en: Would you mind closing the window?

entries.title: Tense backshifting for distance
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Reported speechdagi backshift ham, politeness past ham vaqt emas, masofa/ehtiyotkorlikni bildirishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Past-marked forms can signal reporting distance or politeness as well as chronological past time.
entries.pattern: I hoped you could help
entries.tipUz: Every past-marked clause o‘tgan hodisa emas.

examples.en: I thought you might be interested.
examples.uz: Sizga qiziq bo‘lishi mumkin deb o‘ylagandim.

examples.en: I hoped you could explain this.
examples.uz: Buni tushuntira olasiz deb umid qilgandim.

examples.en: Did you want to ask a question?

entries.title: Habitual will and would
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Will ba’zan odatiy xulq yoki xarakterni bildiradi; would eski takrorlanadigan holat.
entries.explanationEn: Habitual will/would can characterise repeated behaviour, so future time is not their only interpretation.
entries.pattern: She'll often stay late; He would always complain
entries.tipUz: Future meaning deb noto‘g‘ri talqin qilmang.

examples.en: He'll sit for hours reading.
She will often work late.
As children, we would play outside.

entries.title: Focus particles
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Even, merely, simply, just, only, also, too, either, alone farqni nozik o‘zgartiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Focus particles restrict or add emphasis to a particular part of the message; their position matters.
entries.pattern: even X; only X; X alone
entries.tipUz: Fokus zarrachasi noto‘g‘ri o‘rinda bo‘lsa ma’no o‘zgaradi.

examples.en: Even the most experienced staff made mistakes.
examples.uz: Hatto eng tajribali xodimlar ham xato qildi.

examples.en: Even Ali understood.
Ali alone understood.

entries.title: Scope of quantifiers
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Every...not, not every..., few, hardly any, almost all, at least/at most ko‘lamni boshqaradi.
entries.explanationEn: Quantifier scope changes the strength and extent of a claim; not every and none are logically different.
entries.pattern: Not every X is Y; None of X is Y
entries.tipUz: Not every ≠ none; ko‘lamni aralashtirmang.

examples.en: Not every measure was effective.
examples.uz: Har bir chora ham samarali bo‘lavermadi.

examples.en: Almost all the students passed.
At least three students passed.

entries.title: Anaphoric and cataphoric reference
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Olmosh oldingi (anaphora) yoki keyingi (cataphora) ma’lumotga ishora qiladi; tushunarli antecedent tanlang.
entries.explanationEn: Anaphoric reference points back and cataphoric reference points forward; the intended antecedent must be recoverable.
entries.pattern: When she arrived, Mary sat down
entries.tipUz: “It” qaysi otga qaytayotgani noaniq bo‘lmasin.

examples.en: Although it was costly, the scheme continued.
examples.uz: Qimmat bo‘lsa ham dastur davom etdi.

examples.en: Lola arrived, and she sat down.
Before she spoke, Lola checked her notes.

entries.title: Ellipsis in response turns
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “Could do”, “Might have”, “Shouldn't have”, “I hope so”, “I suppose not” qisqa dialog javoblari tabiiy.
entries.explanationEn: Short response turns can omit recoverable material while retaining the right auxiliary or clausal substitute.
entries.pattern: A: Will it work? B: It might.
entries.tipUz: “I hope it” emas; “I hope so”.

examples.en: I hope so.
Will she come? She might.
Have you finished? I have.

entries.title: Situational ellipsis
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “Sounds good”, “Seen John?”, “Any ideas?” kabi to‘liq bo‘lmagan shakllar norasmiy nutqda tabiiy.
entries.explanationEn: Situational ellipsis can be natural in informal interaction, but is not automatically suitable for formal prose.
entries.pattern: (That) sounds good; (Have you) seen John?
entries.tipUz: IELTS academic writingda bunday fragmentlarni odatda ishlatmang.

examples.en: Sounds reasonable to me.
Any questions?
Looks good to me.

entries.title: Dislocation: right/left
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “That book, I loved it” yoki “He's brilliant, your brother” conversationda mavzu va urg‘uni tashkil qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Spoken dislocation can introduce or recall a topic using an extra noun phrase and a corresponding pronoun.
entries.pattern: Topic, pronoun + clause / clause, tag noun
entries.tipUz: Rasmiy essayda bunday dislocation g‘ayrioddiy.

examples.en: My neighbour, she's incredibly helpful.
That film, I really enjoyed it.
She is very kind, your teacher.

entries.title: Tail questions vs tags
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “It's expensive, this place”, “You're coming, right?” so‘zlashuvga xos; canonical question tags bilan farqlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Conversational tails and confirmation expressions differ from canonical auxiliary-pronoun tags in structure and use.
entries.pattern: Statement, right? / statement, isn't it?
entries.tipUz: Intonatsiya ohangni belgilaydi.

examples.en: That's impressive, isn't it?
You are coming, right?
It is busy, this place.

entries.title: Discourse markers grammar
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Well, actually, I mean, you know, mind you, anyway, after all muloqotga signallar beradi.
entries.explanationEn: Discourse markers organise a conversation or express stance; their meaning and formality vary with use.
entries.pattern: Well, + clause; After all, + clause
entries.tipUz: Bu so‘zlar har doim bir xil ma’noda emas; yozma/o‘gzaki registr farq qiladi.

examples.en: Actually, I'd frame the issue differently.
Well, I am not sure.
Anyway, let us continue.

entries.title: Phrasal verb register
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Put off=postpone, look into=investigate, bring about=cause kabi ma’nodoshlar stilistik jihatdan farqli.
entries.explanationEn: A phrasal verb and a single-word alternative may differ in register without every phrasal verb being informal.
entries.pattern: look into the matter / investigate the matter
entries.tipUz: Har phrasal verb norasmiy emas, ko‘pi akademik tilda ham bor.

examples.en: The reform brought about significant change.
We put off the meeting.
The team will look into the issue.

entries.title: Colligation and selection
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: So‘z grammatik qolipni tanlaydi: capable of doing; prone to doing; insist that...; rely on... .
entries.explanationEn: Colligation concerns a word's preferred grammatical company; grammatical form and lexical meaning need to fit together.
entries.pattern: prone to + V-ing; capable of + V-ing
entries.tipUz: Grammatik to‘g‘ri, lekin collocation g‘alati bo‘lsa native eshitilmaydi.

examples.en: The system is capable of handling peak demand.
examples.uz: Tizim eng yuqori talabni ko‘tara oladi.

examples.en: She is capable of solving it.
We rely on accurate information.

entries.title: Determiner precision
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: A certain, a particular, any, whichever, whatever, no, one, another, the other, other, others murakkab referensni ifodalaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Determiners and pronouns identify different relationships among options or sets; other and others do not occupy the same slot.
entries.pattern: another one; the other two; others
entries.tipUz: “Other” determiner va “others” pronoun farqlanadi.

examples.en: One option is cheaper; the other is faster.
We need another chair.
Some stayed; the others left.

entries.title: Generic singular they
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Shaxsi noma’lum yoki o‘zini they deb ifodalovchi odam uchun birlik they tabiiy; fe’l plural morphology oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Singular they can refer to a person of unspecified gender or a person who uses they, while taking forms such as they are.
entries.pattern: If anyone calls, tell them I'm out
entries.tipUz: “They is” standart emas, hatto referent birlik bo‘lsa ham “they are”.

examples.en: Every student should bring their ID.
examples.uz: Har bir talaba o‘z hujjatini olib kelishi kerak.

examples.en: Someone left their bag.
If a student calls, tell them I am busy.
examples.uz: Bir talaba qo‘ng‘iroq qilsa, bandligimni ayting.

entries.title: Inclusive and respectful references
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: People with disabilities, humankind, chair/chairperson kabi tuzilmalar auditoriya/registrga mos bo‘lishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Respectful reference depends on the person, audience and context; avoid unnecessarily assuming gender or treating one label as universally preferred.
entries.pattern: each person ... they
entries.tipUz: “He”ni default barcha kishilar uchun ishlatish shart emas.

examples.en: Applicants must submit their forms.
Every applicant can explain their needs.
examples.uz: Har bir arizachi o‘z ehtiyojini ayta oladi.

examples.en: The chairperson opened the meeting.

entries.title: Article micro-distinctions
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Go to school (institut/maqsad) va go to the school (bino); in hospital (BrE)/in the hospital (AmE).
entries.explanationEn: Articles in institutional expressions can distinguish participation from a particular place/building, with variation across dialects.
entries.pattern: at university / at the university
entries.tipUz: Article tanlovi ko‘pincha ma’no va dialektga bog‘liq.

examples.en: She is at university.
The children are at school.
I went to the school to meet a teacher.
examples.uz: O‘qituvchi bilan uchrashish uchun maktab binosiga bordim.

entries.title: Lexical aspect and telicity
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Build a house (tugallanish nuqtasi bor) vs run (atelic); for/in time phrases bilan farq ochiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Lexical aspect concerns how an event is conceived, including whether it has an inherent endpoint.
entries.pattern: ran for an hour; built a house in a year
entries.tipUz: “For two hours” yakunlanganini har doim bildirmaydi.

examples.en: She wrote the report in two hours.
examples.uz: U hisobotni ikki soatda yozib tugatdi.

examples.en: He ran for an hour.
They built the house in a year.
examples.uz: Ular uyni bir yilda qurib bitirdi.

entries.title: Event structure and argument omission
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Eat/read/teach kabi fe’llar objectni kontekstda tashlashi mumkin, explain/discuss kabi fe’llarda boshqaruv cheklangan.
entries.explanationEn: Some verbs allow an understood object, while others select specific complement patterns; omission depends on sense and context.
entries.pattern: She is reading; discuss the issue
entries.tipUz: “Discuss about the proposal” odatda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: We discussed the proposal.
She is reading.
Please explain the rule to me.

entries.title: Affectedness and voice choice
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Agentni yashirish, neytral jarayon, mas’uliyatni ajratish uchun passive; aniqlik uchun active.
entries.explanationEn: Voice choice changes the presentation of participants and responsibility; passive grammar alone does not justify omitting an important actor.
entries.pattern: Mistakes were made / The team made mistakes
entries.tipUz: Passive agentni yashirishi mumkin; dalil talab etiladigan joyda kimligini yozing.

examples.en: The records were misplaced.
The team lost the file.
The file was lost.

entries.title: Dense noun phrases vs clarity
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “The rapid post-pandemic expansion of services” ixcham, lekin uzun otli zanjirlar ambiguity keltiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Dense noun phrases can compress information but make relationships harder to interpret; expand them when clarity improves.
entries.pattern: a rise in the cost of living
entries.tipUz: To‘rt-besh otni izohsiz ketma-ket tiqmang.

examples.en: The increased cost of living affected low-income families.
examples.uz: Yashash xarajatining oshishi kam daromadli oilalarga ta’sir qildi.

examples.en: The sharp rise in transport costs surprised us.
examples.uz: Transport xarajatining keskin oshishi bizni hayratlantirdi.

examples.en: Transport costs rose sharply, surprising us.
examples.uz: Transport xarajati keskin oshdi va bu bizni hayratlantirdi.

entries.title: Right-branching and end-weight
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Uzun izohlarni gap oxirida berish tabiiy oqim yaratadi; “heavy NP shift” bilan katta object keyinga o‘tadi.
entries.explanationEn: End-weight commonly places longer or more complex material later, while keeping the basic clause relationship easy to follow.
entries.pattern: I explained to the committee the reason ...
entries.tipUz: Og‘ir clause’ni fe’ldan yiroqlashtirmang.

examples.en: They announced a decision that surprised everyone.
examples.uz: Ular barchani hayratda qoldirgan qarorni e’lon qildi.

examples.en: We explained to the group the changes that would affect them.
examples.uz: Guruhga ularga ta’sir qiladigan o‘zgarishlarni tushuntirdik.

examples.en: It is important to review the evidence before deciding.
examples.uz: Qaror qilishdan oldin dalillarni ko‘rish muhim.

entries.title: Apposition and supplements
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “My colleague, a linguist, ...” tushuntiruvchi appositive; restrictive apposition vergulsiz bo‘lishi ham mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Apposition supplies a second noun phrase identifying or describing a referent; punctuation distinguishes supplementary and restrictive uses.
entries.pattern: Dr Smith, an expert in syntax, ...
entries.tipUz: Vergul referentning ma’nosini o‘zgartirishi mumkin.

examples.en: Our teacher, a former examiner, explained the rule.
My friend Lola called.
examples.uz: Do‘stim Lola qo‘ng‘iroq qildi; qaysi do‘stligi aniqlashtirilgan.

examples.en: Lola, my oldest friend, called.
examples.uz: Lola, eng eski do‘stim, qo‘ng‘iroq qildi.

entries.title: Rhetorical questions
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Grammatik so‘roq, lekin maqsad javob emas, ta’sir; akademik IELTSda o‘rinli ishlatish cheklangan.
entries.explanationEn: A rhetorical question is used for communicative effect rather than simply requesting information; context distinguishes it from a genuine question.
entries.pattern: How could we ignore ...?
entries.tipUz: Har paragrafni ritorik savol bilan boshlamang.

examples.en: How could we ignore such clear evidence?
examples.uz: Bunchalik aniq dalilni qanday qilib e’tiborsiz qoldiramiz? — bu yerda ritorik e’tiroz.

examples.en: Who would not want a safer road?
examples.uz: Kim xavfsizroq yo‘lni xohlamaydi? — javob kutmaydigan ta’kid.

examples.en: Why ignore such clear evidence?
examples.uz: Bunchalik aniq dalilni nega e’tiborsiz qoldirish kerak? — ritorik e’tiroz.

entries.title: Metadiscourse and stance
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: This essay argues, to an extent, arguably, from this perspective kabi strukturali signal muallifning pozitsiyasini ko‘rsatadi.
entries.explanationEn: Metadiscourse guides readers through an argument, while stance expressions communicate commitment; neither replaces supporting evidence.
entries.pattern: It could be argued that ...
entries.tipUz: “Arguably” dalil o‘rniga o‘tmaydi.

examples.en: Arguably, the benefits outweigh the risks.
This essay examines two possible causes.
examples.uz: Bu insho ikki ehtimoliy sababni ko‘rib chiqadi.

examples.en: From this perspective, the change is useful.

entries.title: BrE/AmE grammar variation
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Got/gotten, have got/have, collective agreement, preposition use va present perfect tanlovi dialektga qarab o‘zgaradi.
entries.explanationEn: English varieties can differ in grammar as well as vocabulary; choose coherent forms appropriate to the context.
entries.pattern: BrE: I've just eaten; AmE: I just ate (ham mumkin)
entries.tipUz: Bitta dialektni doimiy tanlash izchillik beradi; har ikkisi ko‘p holatda qabul qilinadi.

examples.en: The team is winning.
I have just eaten.
I just ate.
examples.uz: Hozirgina ovqatlandim; Amerikancha inglizchada ham odatiy.

entries.title: Prescriptive vs descriptive grammar
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: “Never end a sentence with a preposition” universal grammatik qoida emas; “Who are you speaking to?” tabiiy.
entries.explanationEn: Distinguish a style preference from a grammatical restriction; descriptive accounts observe real patterns rather than declaring every informal form wrong.
entries.pattern: Who did you speak to? / To whom did you speak?
entries.tipUz: Nima xato, nima uslubiy tanlov ekanini ajrating.

examples.en: That's the person I was talking about.
Who did you speak to?
examples.uz: Siz kim bilan gaplashdingiz? — tabiiy kundalik shakl.

examples.en: To whom did you speak?

entries.title: Punctuation nuance: dash/colon/semicolon
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Em dash kiritma va urg‘u, colon izoh/ro‘yxat, semicolon yaqin mustaqil clause yoki murakkab ro‘yxatlar uchun.
entries.explanationEn: A colon introduces an explanation or expansion, a semicolon links suitable independent clauses, and a dash can mark an interruption or supplement.
entries.pattern: claim: evidence; claim—qualification
entries.tipUz: Punktuatsiya grammatik mazmunni buzmasligi kerak.

examples.en: The choice was clear: invest now or fall behind.
examples.uz: Tanlov ravshan edi: hozir sarmoya qilish yoki ortda qolish.

examples.en: We had one concern: the cost.
The cost was high; the benefit was limited.
examples.uz: Xarajat yuqori edi; foyda esa cheklangan.

entries.title: Spoken rhythm and contraction grammar
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: I'm, we're, would've, hadn't, gonna/wanna (nutq registri) kabi formalar turli rasmiylikda uchraydi.
entries.explanationEn: Contractions interact with spoken rhythm and register; an identical written contraction can expand differently in context.
entries.pattern: I would have → I'd have; going to → gonna (speech)
entries.tipUz: “Gonna” IELTS Writingda tavsiya etilmaydi.

examples.en: I'd have called if I'd known.
I'd like to leave.
examples.uz: Ketishni xohlardim; I'd bu yerda I would.

examples.en: I'd already left when she called.
examples.uz: U qo‘ng‘iroq qilganida allaqachon ketgandim; I'd bu yerda I had.

entries.title: Intonation changes grammar meaning
entries.chapter: 07  C2  |  Nativega yaqin nozik grammatik tanlovlar
entries.explanationUz: Question tag ko‘tariluvchi ohangda haqiqiy savol, tushuvchi ohangda tasdiq izlash; urg‘u fokusni o‘zgartiradi.
entries.explanationEn: Intonation and stress can change the communicative force of an unchanged written sentence; text alone does not establish the actual delivery.
entries.pattern: You're coming, AREN'T you?
entries.tipUz: Transkripsiyasiz faqat yozuv orqali intonatsiyani to‘liq o‘rganib bo‘lmaydi.

examples.en: You did finish it, didn't you?
You finished it, didn't you?
examples.uz: Tugatdingiz, shundaymi? — ohang savol yoki tasdiq kutishni bildiradi.

examples.en: You DID finish it.

entries.title: Common/proper/abstract/collective nouns
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Umumiy va atoqli, mavhum va jamlovchi otlar article va agreement tanloviga ta’sir qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Noun categories can overlap and affect articles/agreement; proper names are not invariably article-free.
entries.pattern: honesty (abstract), the committee (collective)
entries.tipUz: Proper noun har doim articlesiz emas: the Amazon.

examples.en: Honesty is important.
The committee meets today.
Patience is useful.

entries.title: Compound nouns and plurals
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Toothbrush, mother-in-law, passer-by kabi qo‘shma otlarda ko‘plik head qismiga o‘tishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Compound plurals depend on the compound's grammatical head and conventional form, not always on its last written word.
entries.pattern: mothers-in-law; passers-by
entries.tipUz: “Mother-in-laws” odatiy standart ko‘plik emas.

examples.en: Two passers-by stopped to help.
Two mothers-in-law attended.
The car doors were open.

entries.title: Irregular plural families
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Men/women/children/feet/teeth/geese/mice; analysis→analyses; phenomenon→phenomena; criterion→criteria.
entries.explanationEn: Irregular plurals include inherited patterns and borrowed forms; academic singular/plural distinctions can remain important.
entries.pattern: one criterion / several criteria
entries.tipUz: “One criteria” akademik uslubda xato.

examples.en: These criteria are relevant.
One analysis is missing.
Several analyses are available.

entries.title: Uncountables in academic English
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Research, evidence, equipment, legislation, knowledge, data kabi otlar son va dialektdan ta’sirlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Academic mass nouns such as evidence and equipment do not take ordinary count plurals in their usual senses; data varies by usage.
entries.pattern: some evidence; pieces of equipment
entries.tipUz: “Evidences” oddiy mass noun ma’nosida noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: The evidence is compelling.
This research is important.
We need more equipment.

entries.title: Measure and partitive nouns
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: A slice of bread, a grain of rice, a pair of scissors, two litres of water birlikni o‘lchashga xizmat qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Partitives and measures individuate or quantify mass/plural expressions; agreement follows the full construction.
entries.pattern: a piece of + uncountable
entries.tipUz: Scissors ko‘pincha plural agreement oladi.

examples.en: We purchased two pieces of equipment.
She gave me a piece of advice.
She bought two litres of water.

entries.title: Noun–noun modification
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Ot boshqa otni aniqlaganda ko‘pincha singular: a shoe shop, a car door; exceptions: sports centre.
entries.explanationEn: A noun used as a premodifier is often singular, but conventional exceptions prevent an absolute rule.
entries.pattern: a research project / a data set
entries.tipUz: “Transport's policy” har doim mos emas.

examples.en: The transport policy changed.
The school library is open.
We visited a sports centre.

entries.title: Double genitives
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: A friend of my mother's / a friend of mine ikki turli egalik belgisi bilan individual a’zoni bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: A double genitive can identify a member of someone's associated set, using of plus a possessive form.
entries.pattern: a colleague of Sara's
entries.tipUz: “A friend of me” emas.

examples.en: A friend of mine lives nearby.
She is a colleague of my father's.
That book of yours is useful.

entries.title: Possessive of vs 's
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: The roof of the house; the company's policy. Jonli/jonsiz cheklovi absolyut emas; uzunlik va registr ahamiyatli.
entries.explanationEn: Of-genitives and possessive genitives overlap; animacy alone is not an absolute rule for choosing between them.
entries.pattern: the end of the day; today's news
entries.tipUz: “The house's roof” mutlaq xato emas, lekin ko‘pincha “the roof of the house” tabiiyroq.

examples.en: Today's meeting was productive.
The company's office is nearby.
The end of the road is visible.

entries.title: Pronoun case after be/as/than
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: It is I / it's me; taller than I am / taller than me. Birinchilari formal, ikkinchilari kundalik.
entries.explanationEn: Pronoun case after be/as/than depends on construction and register; common spoken object forms are not always errors.
entries.pattern: It was me (normal spoken); It was I (very formal)
entries.tipUz: “Than me” oddiy nutqda keng qabul qilinadi.

examples.en: She's taller than I am.
It was me.
He is older than I am.

entries.title: Reciprocal pronouns
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Each other va one another o‘zaro harakat bildiradi; ikki/koplik bo‘yicha qat’iy chegarasi yo‘q.
entries.explanationEn: Reciprocal pronouns describe an action between participants, unlike reflexives directed back to the same participant.
entries.pattern: help each other
entries.tipUz: Reflexive themselves va reciprocal each other boshqa ma’no.

examples.en: They respect one another.
We help each other.
They looked at themselves in the mirror.

entries.title: Indefinite pronouns
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Something/anything/nothing/everything; somebody/anybody/nobody/everybody singular agreement oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Indefinite pronouns such as everyone and nobody normally take singular verbal agreement even when later they refers back.
entries.pattern: Nobody is; everyone has
entries.tipUz: “Everybody know” emas.

examples.en: Nobody knows the answer.
Everybody has a question.
Something is missing.

entries.title: One, you, we generic subjects
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Umumiy odamlar haqida: one (formal), you (spoken), we (inclusive); grammatik subject tanlovi ohangni boshqaradi.
entries.explanationEn: Generic one, you and we frame general reference with different register and inclusion effects; keep subsequent pronouns consistent.
entries.pattern: One should ...; You never know ...
entries.tipUz: “One ... your” referent nomuvofiqligi bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: One must consider the context.
You learn by practising.
examples.uz: Odam mashq qilib o‘rganadi; bu umumiy you.

examples.en: We all make mistakes.

entries.title: Predeterminers and fractions
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Both/all/half oldin, one-third/two-thirds of dan keyingi otga qarab singular/plural.
entries.explanationEn: Fractions with of commonly take agreement reflecting the quantified noun; predeterminers also have ordering constraints.
entries.pattern: half the students; a third of the water
entries.tipUz: “Two-thirds of the water are” emas (water singular mass).

examples.en: Two-thirds of the students are present.
Half the water is gone.
Half the students are here.

entries.title: No vs not any
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: No + noun (no time) va not any + noun (don't have any time) semantik yaqin, urg‘usi farq qiladi.
entries.explanationEn: No plus a noun and not…any can express related negative meanings, with different placement and emphasis.
entries.pattern: no money / not any money
entries.tipUz: “No evidences” oddiy foydalanishda noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: We have no evidence.
There is no time.
We do not have any chairs.

entries.title: Another, other, others, the other
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Another + singular count; other + plural/uncountable; others mustaqil pronoun; the other aniq qolgani.
entries.explanationEn: Another, other, others and the other differ in number, definiteness and whether they modify or replace a noun.
entries.pattern: another option; other options; the others
entries.tipUz: “Other agreed” ega sifatida noaniq.

examples.en: Some agreed; others disagreed.
Could I have another cup?
The other door is locked.

entries.title: Articles with meals/diseases/seasons
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Have breakfast (umumiy), a delicious breakfast (tasvir), the breakfast we had; the flu, malaria, in winter.
entries.explanationEn: Articles with meals and similar expressions depend on ordinary activity, description and specific reference.
entries.pattern: have lunch / have a quick lunch
entries.tipUz: Article tanlovi otning aniq yoki tasviriy ekaniga bog‘liq.

examples.en: We had a late dinner.
We had breakfast early.
The breakfast you made was delicious.

entries.title: Articles with media/technology
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: The internet, television (medium), the television (device), go online kabi birikmalar an’anaviy shaklga ega.
entries.explanationEn: Media and technology expressions have conventional article patterns and may distinguish a medium from a physical device.
entries.pattern: watch television / fix the television
entries.tipUz: “On internet” standart inglizchada kamroq tabiiy.

examples.en: She works on the internet.
We watch television in the evening.
The television in my room is old.

entries.title: Number and percentage agreement
entries.chapter: 08  QO‘SHIMCHA 1  |  Ot va olmosh tizimining to‘liqroq xaritasi
entries.explanationUz: Forty per cent of the population is ...; forty per cent of residents are ...; head nounga ergashing.
entries.explanationEn: Percentage and majority agreement depends on the quantified noun and construction, with some variation in collective expressions.
entries.pattern: 20% of the money is ...; 20% of people are ...
entries.tipUz: “A majority” bilan kelishuv foydalanishga qarab farqlanishi mumkin.

examples.en: A majority of voters support the change.
Twenty per cent of the money is missing.
Twenty per cent of the students are absent.

entries.title: Adjective order
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Opinion–size–age–shape–colour–origin–material–purpose–noun umumiy heuristika; har kombinatsiya tabiiy emas.
entries.explanationEn: Adjective order follows useful tendencies, not an unrestricted mathematical formula; conventional combinations still matter.
entries.pattern: a lovely small old wooden table
entries.tipUz: Adjective order har doim matematik formula emas, idiomatik cheklovlar bor.

examples.en: She bought a beautiful blue silk scarf.
examples.uz: U chiroyli ko‘k ipak sharf oldi.

examples.en: He bought a small wooden desk.
They live in a beautiful old house.

entries.title: Attributive-only adjectives
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Main, former, mere, elder kabi sifatlar ayrim ma’noda faqat noun oldida keladi.
entries.explanationEn: Some adjective senses are normally attributive, appearing before a noun rather than after a linking verb.
entries.pattern: the main reason; my elder sister
entries.tipUz: “The reason is main” tabiiy emas.

examples.en: This is the main concern.
She is a former teacher.
We discussed the main problem.

entries.title: Predicative-only adjectives
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Afraid, asleep, alive, aware kabi sifatlar predicative holatda ko‘p ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Certain adjectives are normally predicative in their ordinary senses; use an appropriate attributive alternative when needed.
entries.pattern: The child is asleep
entries.tipUz: “An asleep child” o‘rniga “a sleeping child”.

examples.en: The patient is aware of the risk.
The baby is asleep.
We saw a sleeping baby.

entries.title: Gradable vs non-gradable
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Fairly/very/rather bilan oddiy sifatlar; absolutely/completely bilan extreme/adjectives; istisno ko‘p.
entries.explanationEn: Degree expressions should fit the adjective's intended scale or extreme meaning; context and conventional usage permit exceptions.
entries.pattern: very cold / absolutely freezing
entries.tipUz: “Completely very cold” ortiqcha.

examples.en: The task is virtually impossible.
It is very cold.
The answer is completely wrong.

entries.title: Adverb forms and irregulars
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Good→well; fast→fast; hard→hard; late→late; hardly/lately alohida ma’no.
entries.explanationEn: Some adverbs share an adjective's form, while similar -ly forms can have a different meaning.
entries.pattern: drive fast; work hard; hardly work
entries.tipUz: “She speaks good” ayrim dialektlarda uchrasa-da, standart form well.

examples.en: She speaks English well.
He works hard.
He hardly works.

entries.title: Conjunctive vs sentence adverbs
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: However, therefore, consequently, nevertheless mustaqil clause bog‘lanishini ko‘rsatadi, lekin o‘zi oddiy conjunction emas.
entries.explanationEn: Conjunctive adverbs link ideas semantically but do not automatically join two independent clauses with only a comma.
entries.pattern: Clause. However, clause.
entries.tipUz: “Prices rose, however demand...” comma splice bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.en: Prices rose; however, demand remained stable.
examples.uz: Narx oshdi, biroq talab barqaror qoldi.

examples.en: The road was closed. Therefore, we waited.
examples.uz: Yo‘l yopiq edi. Shuning uchun kutdik.

examples.en: It was expensive; nevertheless, we bought it.
examples.uz: U qimmat edi; shunga qaramay sotib oldik.

entries.title: Prepositions of time advanced
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: In two weeks (kelajakda), for two weeks (davomida), within two weeks (ikki haftadan kechikmay), by Friday (jumagacha).
entries.explanationEn: By marks a deadline, until a continuation boundary, for a duration and within an outer time limit.
entries.pattern: by vs until vs within
entries.tipUz: “Until Friday” faoliyat davomiyligi uchun; “by” deadline.

examples.en: Please submit it by Friday.
Finish it by Monday.
I will stay until Monday.

entries.title: Prepositions of place advanced
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: At the door, in the doorway, on the wall, on the bus vs in a car konventional birikmalar.
entries.explanationEn: Place prepositions depend on the relationship and conventional expression, including different transport patterns.
entries.pattern: on a train; in a taxi
entries.tipUz: Hamma transport uchun “in” ishlatilmaydi.

examples.en: She was on the bus when I called.
He is in a taxi.
We met at the door.

entries.title: Preposition stranding
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Relative/wh savol oxiridagi preposition standart va tabiiy; formal variantda oldinga chiqadi.
entries.explanationEn: A stranded preposition can be standard in a wh-question or relative; fronting it often changes the register.
entries.pattern: Who are you talking to? / To whom...?
entries.tipUz: “About which” rasmiy, har doim yaxshiroq degani emas.

examples.en: That's the topic I'm concerned about.
What are you looking at?
The chair I sat on was broken.

entries.title: Dependent adjectives
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Responsible for, capable of, interested in, familiar with, similar to, different from/to (variatsiya) kabi juftlarni yodlang.
entries.explanationEn: Dependent adjectives select conventional prepositions; learn the full combination rather than translating the preposition in isolation.
entries.pattern: responsible for + noun; similar to + noun
entries.tipUz: “Similar with” odatda xato.

examples.en: The approach is similar to ours.
She is responsible for the project.
I am familiar with the area.

entries.title: Dependent nouns
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: An increase in, a reason for, an effect on, a solution to, access to, evidence of.
entries.explanationEn: Dependent noun-preposition combinations encode particular relationships, such as a solution to or an effect on.
entries.pattern: solution to + noun; impact on + noun
entries.tipUz: “Solution of the problem” o‘rniga “solution to the problem”.

examples.en: The rise in demand affected prices.
We need a solution to the problem.
The change had an effect on costs.

entries.title: Multi-word prepositions
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: In spite of, in accordance with, with regard to, by means of, in response to, as a result of.
entries.explanationEn: Multi-word prepositions take a noun phrase or suitable -ing complement; they are not freely interchangeable with conjunctions.
entries.pattern: in accordance with + noun
entries.tipUz: “Due to” va “because of” mosligini kontekst bilan tekshiring.

examples.en: The policy was revised in response to complaints.
We waited because of the rain.
The work followed the plan in accordance with the rules.
examples.uz: Ish qoidalarga muvofiq reja asosida bajarildi.

entries.title: Word derivation
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Prefix va suffix word classni o‘zgartiradi: decide→decision; possible→impossible; happy→happiness.
entries.explanationEn: Derivational affixes can change word class or meaning, but not every imagined derivative is an existing word.
entries.pattern: noun↔verb↔adjective↔adverb
entries.tipUz: “Advise” (verb) va “advice” (noun)ni aralashtirmang.

examples.en: The decision was difficult.
She made a decision.
Their happiness was clear.

entries.title: Compounding and hyphens
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Well-known author (otdan oldin), the author is well known (predicative) farqi; sonli birliklar ham defis oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Attributive compounds often use hyphens and singular measure forms; predicative expressions can have a different form.
entries.pattern: a five-year plan / the plan lasts five years
entries.tipUz: “Five-years plan” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: We adopted a long-term strategy.
It is a three-hour lesson.
The lesson lasts three hours.

entries.title: Irregular spelling of inflections
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Try→tries, study→studied, stop→stopped, make→making, lie→lying, die→dying.
entries.explanationEn: Inflectional spelling includes consonant doubling, y changes and final-e changes, depending on the word and suffix.
entries.pattern: study/studies/studied; run/running
entries.tipUz: “Planing” emas, “planning”.

examples.en: She is planning a trip.
She studies every day.
He is making a cake.

entries.title: Apostrophes
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Possessive: the student's book / students' books; contraction: it's=it is, its=egalik.
entries.explanationEn: Distinguish possessive apostrophes from contractions, especially its/it's and whose/who's.
entries.pattern: it's / its; who's / whose
entries.tipUz: “Its'” standart shakl emas.

examples.en: Its colour has changed.
It's a useful tool.
examples.uz: Bu foydali vosita; it's — it is.

examples.en: The students' books are ready.

entries.title: Capitalisation conventions
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: Countries, languages, weekdays, months, titles, institutions nomining bir qismi, headingsning stylelari.
entries.explanationEn: Capitalisation follows language conventions and style, not the capitalisation rules of another language.
entries.pattern: English, Monday, November
entries.tipUz: Fasllar odatda lowercase: winter.

examples.en: She speaks English and Uzbek.
The course starts in November.
We meet on Tuesday.

entries.title: Numbers, dates and units
entries.chapter: 09  QO‘SHIMCHA 2  |  Sifat, ravish, old ko‘makchi va so‘z yasalishi
entries.explanationUz: a 10-year-old child; ten years old; 25 per cent/25%; ko‘plik va hyphen nuanslari.
entries.explanationEn: Units in attributive measure compounds are usually singular and hyphenated, unlike ordinary plural measure phrases.
entries.pattern: a three-hour exam / three hours
entries.tipUz: “Three-hours exam” emas.

examples.en: The exam lasts three hours.
She is a ten-year-old student.
The journey took two hours.

entries.title: Finite vs non-finite
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Finite fe’l zamon/shaxsni ko‘rsatadi; infinitive/participle/gerund non-finite.
entries.explanationEn: Finite verbs anchor tense/agreement, while non-finite clauses can function inside larger constructions without their own finite marking.
entries.pattern: She wants to leave; Leaving early helps
entries.tipUz: Bitta gap ichida barcha fe’llar finite bo‘lishi shart emas.

examples.en: To understand the issue takes time.
She hopes to win.
Learning takes time.

entries.title: Transitive/intransitive/ditransitive
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Fe’l nechta va qaysi turdagi to‘ldiruvchi olishini belgilaydi.
entries.explanationEn: Verb valency describes permitted object/complement patterns; it can vary between senses of the same verb.
entries.pattern: sleep (no object); discuss a plan; give someone a book
entries.tipUz: “Arrive the station” emas, “arrive at the station”.

examples.en: She gave me a book.
The baby slept.
We discussed the plan.

entries.title: Linking verbs
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Seem, become, remain, look, feel, sound subject complement bilan bog‘laydi; ko‘pincha sifat oladi.
entries.explanationEn: Linking verbs connect a subject to a complement describing or identifying it; ordinary adjective complements are not manner adverbs.
entries.pattern: S + linking verb + adjective
entries.tipUz: “Sounds promisingly” oddiy complement emas.

examples.en: This sounds promising.
She seems tired.
The soup tastes good.

entries.title: Complex-transitive complements
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Make/consider/find/appoint + object + adjective/noun; objectning holatini yoki nomini bildiradi.
entries.explanationEn: An object complement describes or identifies the object after a suitable complex-transitive verb.
entries.pattern: They made her chair; We found it useful
entries.tipUz: “Consider it as viable” ayrim registrlarda keraksiz as.

examples.en: The committee considered the plan viable.
examples.uz: Qo‘mita rejani amalga oshirish mumkin deb baholadi.

examples.en: The news made her happy.
We found the explanation useful.

entries.title: Complement vs adjunct
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Complement fe’l ma’nosini to‘ldirishga zarur, adjunct qo‘shimcha vaziyat; remove test orqali tekshiring.
entries.explanationEn: A complement is selected by the construction, while an adjunct adds circumstances; simple deletion tests are useful but not infallible.
entries.pattern: put X on Y (place often required)
entries.tipUz: “She placed the document” ko‘p kontekstda to‘liqsiz.

examples.en: She placed the document on the table.
He put the bag on the floor.
examples.uz: U sumkani polga qo‘ydi; joy qismi put bilan kerak.

examples.en: She read quietly after lunch.
examples.uz: U tushlikdan keyin sekin o‘qidi; vaqt va tarz qo‘shimcha hol.

entries.title: Do-support and negation
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Oddiy present/pastda yordamchi yo‘q bo‘lsa do/does/did savol, inkor, urg‘uda ishlatiladi.
entries.explanationEn: Do-support supplies an auxiliary for ordinary simple-tense questions, negatives and emphasis, leaving a base main verb.
entries.pattern: Did + S + V? / S didn't + V
entries.tipUz: “Did checked” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: I did check the report.
Did she arrive?
They did not agree.

entries.title: Negative questions
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Aren't you ...? / Didn't she ...? taxmin, hayrat yoki tasdiq izlash; o‘zbekchaga ohang bilan tarjima qiling.
