entries.explanationEn: Negative questions can express expectation, surprise or a suggestion; English yes/no responses refer to the truth of the proposition.
entries.pattern: Isn't it strange?
entries.tipUz: Negative questionga yes/no javoblar o‘zbekchadan farq qiladi.

examples.en: Didn't you receive my email?
Isn't it cold?
Don't you want to come?

entries.title: Embedded declaratives and questions
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: I know [that ...] / I know [what ...] gap ichidagi clause; unda inversion yo‘q.
entries.explanationEn: Embedded interrogatives use statement order even though they contain a question word and express unknown information.
entries.pattern: wonder why she left
entries.tipUz: “I wonder why did he resign” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: I wonder why he resigned.
She knows where he works.
Tell me what you need.

entries.title: Question words with ever
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Whoever, whatever, whichever, wherever, whenever, however erkin tanlov yoki noma’lumlikni bildirishi mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: Wh-ever forms can express free choice, lack of restriction or concession, with interpretation determined by their construction.
entries.pattern: whoever calls; whatever happens
entries.tipUz: “However” ravish sifatida ham: however difficult.

examples.en: Whatever happens, stay calm.
examples.uz: Nima bo‘lishidan qat’i nazar, xotirjam bo‘ling.

examples.en: Whoever arrives first can start.
You can sit wherever you like.

entries.title: Negative concord and dialect
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: “I didn't see nothing” ayrim dialektlarda tizimli double negation; standard formal Englishda “anything” afzal.
entries.explanationEn: Negative concord is systematic in some dialects, while standard formal English commonly uses any with an existing negative.
entries.pattern: I didn't see anything
entries.tipUz: Dialektni xato deb umumlashtirmang; IELTSda standart registrni tanlang.

examples.en: I didn't see anyone.
We did not find anything.
Nobody called.

entries.title: Neither/nor/not either
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: “Neither did I” va “I didn't either” inkor fikriga qo‘shiladi; not ... neither odatda nonstandard.
entries.explanationEn: Neither/nor inversion and negative…either can express agreement with a negative statement; match the auxiliary.
entries.pattern: Neither do I / I don't either
entries.tipUz: “I don't neither” standart formal emas.

examples.en: I don't agree, and neither does she.
He cannot swim, and neither can I.
She does not drive, and I do not either.
examples.uz: U mashina haydamaydi, men ham haydamayman.

entries.title: Not...until / no longer / not anymore
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Negatsiya vaqt chegarasini bildiradi: not until=...gacha emas, no longer/anymore=endi emas.
entries.explanationEn: Not until delays an event to a boundary; no longer/not anymore describe a situation that has stopped.
entries.pattern: didn't leave until; no longer work here
entries.tipUz: “Until”ni “by” deadline bilan aralashtirmang.

examples.en: We didn't start until noon.
She no longer works here.
We did not leave until the rain stopped.

entries.title: Conditional counterexamples
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: If + will (willingness), if + should, if + would (polite request/insistence) ayrim konstruksiyalarda to‘g‘ri.
entries.explanationEn: Will/would in an if-clause can be appropriate for willingness, insistence or a polite request, unlike a simple future-prediction if-clause.
entries.pattern: If you will wait here ...
entries.tipUz: “If dan keyin hech qachon will kelmaydi” degan qoida haddan tashqari qat’iy.

examples.en: If you'll sign here, we can begin.
If you will wait a moment, I will check.
examples.uz: Bir oz kutib tursangiz, tekshiraman; kutishga rozilik so‘ralyapti.

examples.en: If you would follow me, I will show you the room.
examples.uz: Orqamdan yursangiz, xonani ko‘rsataman; muloyim iltimos.

entries.title: Otherwise/or else/in case
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Otherwise/or else natija-ogohlantirish, in case ehtimoldan ehtiyot chora ko‘rish.
entries.explanationEn: In case commonly motivates a precaution taken before a possible event; otherwise/or else introduces a consequence or alternative.
entries.pattern: Take an umbrella in case it rains
entries.tipUz: In case ≠ if: “in case” chora oldindan bajariladi.

examples.en: Save a copy in case the file gets lost.
Take a coat in case it gets cold.
examples.uz: Sovuq bo‘lib qolsa deb palto oling.

examples.en: Leave now; otherwise, you may be late.
examples.uz: Hozir chiqing; aks holda kechikishingiz mumkin.

entries.title: Whether...or / regardless of
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Ikki ehtimol ham natijani o‘zgartirmasligi uchun whether...or not, regardless of.
entries.explanationEn: Whether…or can present alternatives without changing the main consequence; regardless of takes a suitable nominal complement.
entries.pattern: Whether S V or not, ...
entries.tipUz: Whether va if barcha grammatik muhitda almashtirilmaydi.

examples.en: Whether you agree or not, the rule applies.
Whether it rains or not, we will go.
Everyone can join regardless of age.
examples.uz: Yoshidan qat’i nazar hamma qo‘shilishi mumkin.

entries.title: Comparative as clauses
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: As ... as; not so ... as; as much/many ... as; twice as ... as.
entries.explanationEn: As…as constructions express equality or a specified multiple; keep the compared quantities and units clear.
entries.pattern: twice as many ... as
entries.tipUz: “Two times more” matematik noaniqlik keltirishi mumkin.

examples.en: We have twice as many applicants as last year.
examples.uz: O‘tgan yilga qaraganda ikki baravar ko‘p arizachi bor.

examples.en: This room is twice as large as that one.
examples.uz: Bu xona anavisidan ikki baravar katta.

examples.en: We have as much time as they do.

entries.title: Too/enough + infinitive / for
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Too + adj + for + object + to V; adj + enough + for + object + to V.
entries.explanationEn: Too/enough constructions can include a for-phrase identifying the infinitive's understood subject.
entries.pattern: too difficult for me to solve
entries.tipUz: Subject mantiqini tekshiring.

examples.en: It is easy enough for children to understand.
The box is too heavy for me to lift.
examples.uz: Quti men ko‘tarishim uchun haddan tashqari og‘ir.

examples.en: She is old enough to travel alone.
examples.uz: U yolg‘iz sayohat qiladigan yoshga yetgan.

entries.title: Non-finite negatives
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: Not to do, not having done, not being allowed kabi inkor non-finite birikmaning boshida.
entries.explanationEn: Negation can precede a non-finite phrase; some split infinitives are also grammatical, depending on intended scope and style.
entries.pattern: not to tell; not being invited
entries.tipUz: “To not” ayrim holatda ham mumkin (split infinitive), mutlaq taqiq emas.

examples.en: He regretted not applying earlier.
She decided not to go.
Not knowing the answer, I asked.

entries.title: Split infinitives
entries.chapter: 10  QO‘SHIMCHA 3  |  Fe’l sintaksisi, so‘roq va inkor tuzilmalari
entries.explanationUz: “To fully understand”, “to better support” grammatik va ko‘pincha ravon; “to understand fully” ham mumkin.
entries.explanationEn: An adverb between to and an infinitive is not universally ungrammatical; choose clear scope and natural rhythm.
entries.pattern: to carefully examine / to examine carefully
entries.tipUz: Split infinitive universal xato emas.

examples.en: We aim to fully understand the problem.
We need to carefully check the figures.
She hopes to better understand the issue.
examples.uz: U masalani yaxshiroq tushunishga umid qiladi.

entries.title: Clause vs sentence vs fragment
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Clause ega+kesim tuzilishi, sentence yakunlangan mustaqil birlik; subordinated clause mustaqil har doim emas.
entries.explanationEn: A clause need not be a complete independent sentence; a subordinate fragment may need a main clause in formal prose.
entries.pattern: Because it rained, we stayed.
entries.tipUz: “Because demand fell.” writingda atayin fragment bo‘lmasa xato.

examples.en: Because demand fell, prices declined.
She left because she was tired.
Although it rained, we continued.

entries.title: Coordination vs subordination
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: And/but/or teng, although/because/if qaram; syntactic hierarchy diqqatni boshqaradi.
entries.explanationEn: Coordination connects units at a comparable level; subordination makes one clause dependent on another.
entries.pattern: X, but Y / Although X, Y
entries.tipUz: Ikkita fikrni faqat and bilan bog‘lash argumentni zaiflashtiradi.

examples.en: Although the method is costly, it is effective.
It was cold, but we walked.
Because it was cold, we stayed inside.

entries.title: Reference chains and cohesion
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Aniq noun→this measure/it/the policy kabi qayta nomlash matnni bog‘laydi; sinonimlar referentni buzmasin.
entries.explanationEn: Cohesion relies on clear reference across sentences; repeating or renaming a referent should preserve its identity.
entries.pattern: a reform → the measure → it
entries.tipUz: “This” o‘zi oldingi bir necha fikrga ishora qilsa noaniq.

examples.en: This approach reduces uncertainty.
We introduced a new rule. This rule applies to everyone.
examples.uz: Yangi qoida kiritdik. Bu qoida hammaga tegishli.

examples.en: The plan was revised. It is now simpler.
examples.uz: Reja qayta ko‘rildi. Endi u soddaroq.

entries.title: Given–new information
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Tanilgan ma’lumot odatda oldin, yangisi oxirda keladi; natijada gap osonroq tushuniladi.
entries.explanationEn: Given-new organisation helps readers connect an established topic to the next important piece of information.
entries.pattern: The proposal has one weakness: its cost.
entries.tipUz: Murakkab gap doim yaxshiroq degani emas.

examples.en: A key obstacle is the lack of funding.
We need a solution. The simplest solution is to wait.
examples.uz: Yechim kerak. Eng sodda yechim — kutish.

examples.en: The plan has one weakness: its cost.
examples.uz: Rejaning bitta zaif tomoni bor: xarajati.

entries.title: Theme and rheme
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Matn tema (gap nimaga oid) va rema (nima yangilik) orasidagi mantiqiy rivojga tayangan.
entries.explanationEn: Theme-rheme organisation connects what a clause starts from with what it adds, supporting a coherent progression.
entries.pattern: This change ... / Its consequences ...
entries.tipUz: Har gapni mustaqil, uzilgan fikrga aylantirmang.

examples.en: This increase affects households differently.
examples.uz: Bu oshish xonadonlarga turlicha ta’sir qiladi.

examples.en: The school opened a library. The library now serves the whole town.
examples.uz: Maktab kutubxona ochdi. Kutubxona endi butun shaharchaga xizmat qilyapti.

examples.en: The road was repaired. This improvement reduced delays.
examples.uz: Yo‘l ta’mirlandi. Bu yaxshilanish kechikishlarni kamaytirdi.

entries.title: Hedge vs booster
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Probably/possibly/suggests/may ehtiyotkorlik; clearly/certainly/demonstrates kuchaytiruvchi; dalilga qarab tanlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Hedges and boosters express different commitment strengths; use them in proportion to evidence rather than as decoration.
entries.pattern: may indicate vs demonstrates
entries.tipUz: Correlation ≠ causation: “prove”ni o‘rinsiz ishlatmang.

examples.en: The data indicate a possible association.
The result may suggest a link.
The measurements clearly show a rise in temperature.

entries.title: Cause/result connectors
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Because/as/since + clause; because of/due to + noun; therefore/consequently + separate clause.
entries.explanationEn: Cause/result expressions select different syntax: because plus a clause, because of plus a nominal phrase, therefore linking propositions.
entries.pattern: X; therefore, Y
entries.tipUz: “Because of costs increased” noto‘g‘ri.

examples.en: The cost increased; consequently, demand fell.
We stayed because it rained.
It rained; therefore, we stayed.

entries.title: Addition/contrast connectors
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Furthermore/moreover/in addition/likewise/whereas/by contrast/instead.
entries.explanationEn: Addition and contrast connectors signal different logical relationships; choose one that fits the actual argument.
entries.pattern: Clause. By contrast, clause.
entries.tipUz: “On the other hand” har doim “moreover” sinonimi emas.

examples.en: Urban areas expanded; by contrast, rural populations fell.
examples.uz: Shahar hududlari kengaydi, qishloq aholisi esa kamaydi.

examples.en: The method is cheap. Moreover, it is simple.
examples.uz: Usul arzon. Bundan tashqari, u sodda.

examples.en: She chose the bus; I walked instead.
examples.uz: U avtobusni tanladi; men esa piyoda yurdim.

entries.title: Evidence and exemplification
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: For example, for instance, such as, namely, particularly, in particular tanlangan sintaksisga qarab farqlanadi.
entries.explanationEn: Exemplification expressions have different syntax: such as introduces examples within a phrase, while for example can frame a clause.
entries.pattern: such as + noun phrase; for example, + clause
entries.tipUz: “Such as” ortidan mutlaqo mustaqil xabar gap keltirmang.

examples.en: Some cities, such as Seoul, have dense networks.
examples.uz: Seul kabi ayrim shaharlarda zich tarmoqlar bor.

examples.en: I enjoy outdoor activities, such as walking.
examples.uz: Piyoda yurish kabi ochiq havodagi mashg‘ulotlarni yoqtiraman.

examples.en: Some tasks are difficult. For example, this one takes an hour.
examples.uz: Ayrim vazifalar qiyin. Masalan, bunisi bir soat vaqt oladi.

entries.title: Appositive that vs relative that
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: The fact that prices rose (content clause) va the fact that we noted (relative) bir xil that shaklida, lekin vazifasi boshqa.
entries.explanationEn: A content that-clause states a noun's content; a relative that-clause contains a grammatical gap related to the noun.
entries.pattern: the belief that + S V; the report that + relative
entries.tipUz: Content-clause “that”ni relative sifatida doim tashlab bo‘lmaydi.

examples.en: The claim that taxes reduce consumption is contested.
examples.uz: Soliqlar iste’molni kamaytiradi degan da’vo bahsli.

examples.en: The fact that she left surprised us.
examples.uz: Uning ketgani bizni hayratlantirdi; that qismida mazmun berilgan.

examples.en: The fact that we discussed was important.
examples.uz: Biz muhokama qilgan fakt muhim edi; muhokama obyekti fact.

entries.title: Academic grammar of data
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Fell from X to Y, rose by X%, stood at Y, was twice as high as; farqli predloglar.
entries.explanationEn: Data descriptions distinguish starting point, endpoint and change amount; by and to are not interchangeable.
entries.pattern: increase by 20% / increase to 20%
entries.tipUz: “Rose by 70%” va “rose to 70%” boshqa matematik ma’no.

examples.en: Employment rose from 60% to 70%.
Sales rose by ten per cent.
Sales rose to one hundred units.

entries.title: Numbers and comparatives
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Percentage points va per cent farqi; “twice as high”, “half as much” qiyosiy parallel.
entries.explanationEn: A percentage-point change is the difference between percentages; a percent change is relative to the starting value.
entries.pattern: 20%→30% = +10 percentage points
entries.tipUz: Bu “10% ga oshdi” bilan bir xil emas.

examples.en: The rate increased by ten percentage points.
The rate rose from twenty to thirty per cent.

entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Present simple passive odatda ilmiy jarayon tasvirida; sequencing: first, then, subsequently, finally.

entries.title: Formality ladder
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Kids→children, get worse→deteriorate, a lot of→many/considerable; lekin oddiy so‘z ham to‘g‘ri ishlatilsa kuchli.
entries.explanationEn: Formality concerns suitable lexical and grammatical choices, not the number of difficult words in a sentence.

entries.explanationEn: Maintain a register appropriate to the task; spoken contractions and conversational markers need not be errors.

entries.title: Sentence boundaries
entries.chapter: 11  QO‘SHIMCHA 4  |  Matn grammatikasi va rasmiy uslub
entries.explanationUz: Independent clause’larni nuqta/semicolon/conjunction bilan ajrating; run-on va comma splice xatolarini toping.
entries.explanationEn: Independent clauses need an appropriate boundary or connector; a comma alone usually creates a comma splice.
entries.pattern: X. Y. / X, and Y. / X; Y.
entries.tipUz: “Results improved, the plan succeeded” comma splice.

examples.en: The results were promising, but further tests are required.

examples.en: The rain stopped. We left.
The rain stopped, so we left.

entries.explanationEn: The serial comma is a style choice that can help clarity; quotation punctuation also varies by convention.

entries.tipUz: Oxford comma hamma uslubda majburiy emas.
